## Docs

### What is SDP?
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/introduction

> One API for building on Solana with your chosen providers, from devnet to mainnet.

Solana Developer Platform (SDP) gives your app one API for the Solana services it uses. Build and test on devnet in the dashboard, then call the API with a key you create there.

## Why SDP

Institutional assets are moving onchain. In October 2026, RWA.xyz tracked [about $39.5 billion in tokenized real-world assets](https://app.rwa.xyz/), including [about $5.2 billion on Solana](https://app.rwa.xyz/networks/solana). [Tokenized stocks](https://app.rwa.xyz/stocks) are one part of that growth.

Assets at this scale need custody, enforceable compliance, and auditable controls. SDP puts the services your deployment supports behind one API, so you can build on Solana without wiring up every provider yourself.

## How it fits together

- **Devnet and mainnet** each have their own keys, wallets, and settings. Build on devnet with test tokens, then [go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) once SDP approves your organization.
- **Providers** supply the services behind SDP. You choose the providers you use; your app calls the same SDP API either way.
- **Access** is explicit. An API key holds only the actions you grant it, and sensitive operations leave an audit trail.

## What you can build

This deployment publishes these modules:

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Issuance** | Deploy, mint, burn, freeze, pause, and seize tokens built on Token-2022 |
| **Custody** | Provision and operate Solana wallets through interchangeable custody providers |
| **Payments** | Move funds onchain: transfers, batches, recurring payments, and payment requests |
| **Ramps** | Move between fiat and onchain funds through interchangeable ramp providers |
| **Earn** | Discover DeFi and RWA strategies for customer-wallet deposits and withdrawals |
| **Compliance** | Screen wallets and transactions against your regulatory program |
| **Asset profiles** | Issued-asset identity and metadata, and the public token metadata URI |

[Get started](/docs) on devnet, or [browse the API reference](/docs/reference/api).

### Go to mainnet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet

> Request mainnet access, connect your own custody account, and go live.

You start with a Sandbox project on devnet. The SDP team must approve your
organization before enabling Production on mainnet.

## 1. Request mainnet access

Sign in to the [dashboard](https://platform.solana.com/dashboard) as an
**organization admin**. Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then
**Settings**. Under **Mainnet access**, click **Request mainnet access**. If the
section is missing, ask an admin to submit.

[![The Mainnet access section in organization settings, with Request mainnet access](/images/go-to-mainnet/01-request-access.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/01-request-access.png)

Select your organization's registered **Country or region** and click
**Continue**. Contact the SDP team to change it after submission.

[![Request mainnet access with Singapore selected as the organization's jurisdiction](/images/go-to-mainnet/02-jurisdiction.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/02-jurisdiction.png)

Read the **Terms and Conditions** to the end, accept them on your organization's
behalf, and click **Send request**. **Request sent** confirms submission;
Settings shows **In review** until approval.

[![Request sent confirmation, with SDP review still pending](/images/go-to-mainnet/request-sent.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/request-sent.png)

If you see **Request not sent**, click **Send request again**; your details are
saved. If requests aren't open, contact the SDP team.

## 2. Switch to Production

After approval, refresh **Settings**. When **Mainnet access** shows **Approved**,
click your organization's name at the top of the sidebar and select your
production project (by default, **Default Production Project**).

<a href="/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/03-production-project.png">
  <img
    src="/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/03-production-project.png"
    alt="The workspace switcher showing Default Production Project"
    width="330"
    height="342"
    style={{ maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto" }}
  />
</a>

Production uses `mainnet-beta`. Wallets, provider connections, and API keys are
separate from Sandbox and must be set up again.

## 3. Connect your custody provider account

Production runs on your own provider account. Open **Wallets**, click
**Create wallet**, and choose a provider.

- [Connect Fireblocks](/docs/wallet-operations/fireblocks): Connect your own Fireblocks workspace for production custody.

For Privy, keep or rename the **Credential label**. Enter your **Privy app ID** and
**Privy app secret** from the [Privy dashboard](https://dashboard.privy.io),
then a **Wallet label**. Click **Connect and create wallet** to verify the
connection and create your first Privy wallet.

[![Privy credential form with an example app ID and a masked app secret](/images/go-to-mainnet/04-connect-privy.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/04-connect-privy.png)

For more wallets, pick this connection under **Whose Privy account holds the
keys?** See [Create a wallet](/docs/guides/setup-wallets).

## 4. Create a production API key

In Production, open **API keys** and click **Create new API key**. Name it,
grant the actions it needs, choose which wallets it can sign with, and review
the summary. Click **Create key**.

[![API key review showing Production, selected permissions, and the Treasury wallet](/images/go-to-mainnet/05-production-api-key.png)](/docs/images/go-to-mainnet/05-production-api-key.png)

Copy the key to your secret manager; it's shown once. Replace your backend's
sandbox key. The API URL stays `https://api.solana.com`; the key's project
determines the network. See
[API key grants and wallet access](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys).

## 5. Fund your wallet with mainnet USDC

Send a small amount of **USDC on Solana mainnet** to your wallet's address.
Devnet tokens have no value on mainnet. Circle's
[mainnet USDC mint](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses)
is `EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v`.

Use `"token": "USDC"` in transfer requests so SDP selects the mint for your network.
Replace any hardcoded devnet mint addresses.

SDP sponsors network fees and recipient token-account rent for transfers it
signs from your Privy wallet. Fund it with USDC; no SOL is needed for those fees.
Sponsorship limits apply. If sponsorship is unavailable, SDP refuses the transfer
instead of charging your wallet.

Send a [small first payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment) and
[verify its status](/docs/payments/accept-verification) before increasing volume.

### Core concepts
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp

> The interfaces, environments, and conventions you build against.

SDP has two interfaces over the same API:

- **Dashboard:** the browser UI. Sign in with email, Google, or GitHub.
- **REST API:** programmatic access for backend integrations. Requests authenticate with an API key in the `Authorization` header.

Both call the same API, and each route requires the same action whoever calls it. A signed-in member holds actions through their organization role; an API key holds the grants you give it. Some routes are for signed-in members only, such as managing API keys, members, and the organization, or setting up a custody provider. An API key is refused them.

Build against the API for automation and integrations. Use the dashboard to set up your organization, inspect state, and run one-off operations.

## Environments

An environment belongs to the **project**, not to individual requests. Every tenant resource and API key belongs to a project and inherits its environment.

| Environment  | Network      |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| `sandbox`    | devnet       |
| `production` | mainnet-beta |

A key's format doesn't name its environment; the project it belongs to does.

Both environments expose the same route shapes. Build and test against your sandbox project, then move to production with a production project's API key. [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) covers requesting access and setting up your production wallets and API key.

## Response conventions

Every successful response wraps its payload in a `data` envelope with request metadata:

```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-07-31T12:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Errors return a machine-readable `code` alongside a human-readable `message`:

```json
{
  "error": { "code": "INVALID_API_KEY", "message": "Invalid API key" },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_..." }
}
```

Include the `requestId` when you report an issue. It links your request to SDP's traces.

## Execution model

For a custody operation, SDP builds the transaction, signs it with the configured custody wallet, and submits it.

### Payments
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments

> Send, accept and reconcile Solana payments from your SDP custody wallets.

Send SOL and SPL tokens from your custody wallets, pay many recipients in one batch, schedule recurring payments, and match what moved to your own records. If you have no custody wallet yet, start with [Set Up Wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets).

## What's in this section

- **[How payments work on SDP](/docs/payments/concepts)**: wallets, tokens, fees and the transfer record.
- **Send payments**
  - [Basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment): one transfer, from the dashboard or the API.
  - [Payment with memo](/docs/payments/send-payment-with-memo): tag a transfer with your order or invoice reference.
  - [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts): pay many recipients and reconcile the run.
- **Accept payments**
  - [Accept overview](/docs/payments/accept-overview): payment links, shared addresses, and finding each payment.
  - [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification): transfer statuses and when a payment is final.
  - [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing): list transfers and match them to your ledger.

Wallet balances and controls are in [Wallet operations](/docs/wallet-operations).

## Earn

### Earn
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn

> Offer stablecoin yield in your app, from your customers' own wallets, through one API.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Earn lets your customers earn yield on stablecoins without handing over their
keys. Your backend builds each deposit and withdrawal through SDP, your
customer's wallet signs it, and SDP broadcasts it and tracks it to settlement.

[Start the quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart)

[API reference](/docs/reference/api/earn)

## What you can build

| Capability | What Earn gives you |
| --- | --- |
| [Strategies](/docs/earn/strategies) | A catalog of DeFi and real-world-asset strategies with live rates, deposit tokens, and withdrawal terms. |
| [Deposits](/docs/earn/deposits) | Live quotes, unsigned transactions for your customer's wallet, and tracking from submit to finality. |
| [Balances and earnings](/docs/earn/balances) | Live positions, recorded movements, and exact earnings for each customer wallet. |
| [Withdrawals](/docs/earn/withdrawals) | Instant withdrawals, plus provider orders, solver queues, and operator redemptions that pay out later. |

Returns, losses, fees, and withdrawal timing depend on the strategy. An APY is
a rate, not a promise.

## How it works

- **Customer's wallet**

  Signs a deposit of the strategy's deposit token.

- **Strategy**

  Issues shares or a yield-bearing token to the customer's wallet.

- **Customer's wallet**

  Receives the payout when a withdrawal settles.

SDP never holds your customer's keys or pools their funds in an SDP account.
Funds sit with the strategy's protocol or provider, whose custody and
withdrawal risks still apply. [How Earn works](/docs/earn/concepts) explains
shares, signing, and settlement.

## Start building

Run the [Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart) to make your first sandbox deposit
through the Earn API, then follow [Embedded Yield](/docs/guides/embedded-yield)
to ship the full integration. Every request field and response is in the
[Earn API reference](/docs/reference/api/earn).

### Quickstart
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/quickstart

> Deposit test USDC into a strategy from a sandbox wallet, then read the position, in about ten minutes.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Everything here runs in your sandbox project on devnet, with a local test
wallet standing in for your customer's wallet. Nothing touches real funds.

## Before you begin

Create the project folder. Run the remaining commands from it:

```bash title="Terminal"
mkdir earn-quickstart && cd earn-quickstart
```

| You need | How to get it |
| --- | --- |
| An API URL for a beta or experimental deployment | Use the API URL supplied with your SDP deployment. Stable deployments do not include Earn. |
| A sandbox API key with `earn.execute` | [Create an API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) in your sandbox project. Keep it on your backend. |
| The Solana CLI | [Install it](https://solana.com/docs/intro/installation) for `solana-keygen` and `solana airdrop`. |
| A test wallet | `solana-keygen new --no-bip39-passphrase -o test-wallet.json` creates one. It plays your customer's wallet. |
| Devnet SOL | `solana airdrop 1 $(solana-keygen pubkey test-wallet.json) --url devnet`, or the [Solana faucet](https://faucet.solana.com). The wallet pays network fees and the rent for its new accounts, under 0.004 SOL. |
| Devnet USDC | The [Circle faucet](https://faucet.circle.com) on Solana Devnet. Most sandbox strategies take this mint: `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`. The examples deposit 25, so request enough or lower `amount`. |
| Node.js 20.18 or later | For the TypeScript steps. |

Your organization also needs the strategy's provider activated. If a preview
returns `403` with `provider_not_entitled`, ask your SDP contact.

Install the TypeScript tools, then set your deployment URL and key:

```bash title="Terminal"
npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @solana/kit@8 && npm install -D tsx
export SDP_API_URL="https://YOUR_SDP_API_HOST"
export SDP_API_KEY="sf_..."
```

Then add the test wallet helper. It signs exactly the bytes SDP builds, which
is what your customer's wallet will do in production:

```typescript title="test-wallet.ts"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import {
  createKeyPairFromBytes,
  getAddressFromPublicKey,
  getBase64EncodedWireTransaction,
  getBase64Encoder,
  getTransactionDecoder,
  partiallySignTransaction,
} from "@solana/kit";

// Sandbox only: a local keypair stands in for your customer's wallet.
const secretKey = new Uint8Array(JSON.parse(await readFile("test-wallet.json", "utf8")));
const keyPair = await createKeyPairFromBytes(secretKey);

export const ownerAddress = await getAddressFromPublicKey(keyPair.publicKey);

/** Signs SDP's unsigned base64 transaction without changing it. */
export async function signWithTestWallet(transactionBase64: string): Promise<string> {
  const transaction = getTransactionDecoder().decode(getBase64Encoder().encode(transactionBase64));
  // Partial: it leaves any other signer's slot, such as your fee payer's, empty.
  const signed = await partiallySignTransaction([keyPair], transaction);
  return getBase64EncodedWireTransaction(signed);
}
```

## Make the deposit

Call the Earn API with a small request helper, then write the deposit as one
file, `deposit.ts`.

### 1. Add the request helper

```typescript title="earn-api.ts"
const SDP_API_URL = process.env.SDP_API_URL;
if (!SDP_API_URL) throw new Error("Set SDP_API_URL to your beta or experimental API URL");
const SDP_API_KEY = process.env.SDP_API_KEY;
if (!SDP_API_KEY) throw new Error("Set SDP_API_KEY to your sandbox API key");

/** Calls the Earn API: GET without a body, POST with one. Returns `data`. */
export async function earnRequest(path: string, body?: unknown, idempotencyKey?: string) {
  const response = await fetch(`${SDP_API_URL}${path}`, {
    method: body === undefined ? "GET" : "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${SDP_API_KEY}`,
      ...(body === undefined ? {} : { "Content-Type": "application/json" }),
      ...(idempotencyKey ? { "Idempotency-Key": idempotencyKey } : {}),
    },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`SDP returned ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
  }
  return (await response.json()).data;
}

/** Polls a movement until it is final: every second for a minute, then every five seconds. */
export async function waitForMovement(movementId: string, timeoutMs = 300_000) {
  const startedAt = Date.now();
  while (Date.now() - startedAt < timeoutMs) {
    const { movement } = await earnRequest(
      `/v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/${encodeURIComponent(movementId)}`,
    );
    if (movement.status === "finalized" || movement.status === "failed") return movement;
    const delayMs = Date.now() - startedAt < 60_000 ? 1_000 : 5_000;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
  }
  throw new Error(`Movement ${movementId} is not final yet; keep tracking it`);
}
```

### 2. Choose a strategy, then build

This example picks an active, fundable strategy whose first deposit mint is
devnet USDC and needs no slippage floor.
[Strategies](/docs/earn/strategies) explains each check.

```typescript title="deposit.ts"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { earnRequest, waitForMovement } from "./earn-api";
import { ownerAddress, signWithTestWallet } from "./test-wallet";

type Strategy = {
  id: string;
  status: string;
  fundable: boolean;
  depositMints: string[];
  depositSlippage: unknown;
  withdrawalSlippage: { defaultToleranceBps: number } | null;
};

const { strategies }: { strategies: Strategy[] } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/strategies?pageSize=100",
);
const strategy = strategies.find(
  (s) => s.fundable && s.status === "active" && s.depositSlippage === null
    && s.depositMints[0] === "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
);
if (!strategy) throw new Error("No devnet USDC strategy is open for deposits");
const amount = "25"; // in the deposit token, depositMints[0]

const preview = await earnRequest("/v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews", {
  strategyId: strategy.id,
  amount,
});
if (preview.blockingIssues.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(`Preview blocked: ${JSON.stringify(preview.blockingIssues)}`);
}

const { transaction: built } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions",
  { strategyId: strategy.id, ownerAddress, amount },
);
```

The build is an unsigned transaction. Nothing has moved yet.

### 3. Sign and submit

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const signedTransaction = await signWithTestWallet(built.transaction);

// In production, save the idempotency key with the signed transaction before you send it,
// and retry an uncertain response with both unchanged.
const idempotencyKey = randomUUID();
const { deposit } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits",
  { transactionId: built.transactionId, signedTransaction },
  idempotencyKey,
);
```

SDP checks the signature against the exact bytes it built, records the
deposit, then broadcasts it.

Persist `deposit.positionId` with the selected strategy's `withdrawalSlippage`
in your backend. Save `null` explicitly when no floor is supported. Keep this
record for withdrawals even if the strategy leaves the catalog.

### 4. Track it and read the position

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const movement = await waitForMovement(deposit.movementId);
if (movement.status === "failed") throw new Error(movement.failureReason ?? "Deposit failed");

const { positions } = await earnRequest(
  `/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions?${new URLSearchParams({ ownerAddress })}`,
);
console.log(JSON.stringify(positions, null, 2));
```

Run it:

```bash title="Terminal"
npx tsx deposit.ts
```

## See the result

The movement usually reaches `finalized` within 30 seconds, and the wallet
holds shares in the strategy. Your strategy and its `label` may differ:

```json title="Output (trimmed)"
[
  {
    "id": "earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b",
    "ownerAddress": "Af89Mkuvo6AcLDbs7Fxs1FPsnnbD9KrY9NfmaFXHqmPo",
    "provider": "kamino",
    "label": "Kamino Vault USDC",
    "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
    "shareMint": "CeirL1mAehaM6g2EccgMUQwohNfnuyicskVQ4r9ekXk6",
    "shares": "25",
    "withdrawableShares": "25",
    "tokenValue": "25"
  }
]
```

`tokenValue` is the position's live value in the deposit token. Share and
token amounts are equal here only because this vault's shares are still worth
one USDC each.

## Sign in your customer's wallet

In production, the signing step runs in your app, not on your backend. With a
[Wallet Standard](https://github.com/wallet-standard/wallet-standard) wallet
and `@solana/react` (`npm install @solana/react@8 @solana/kit@8` in your app),
sign the same base64 transaction and check that the wallet returned it
unchanged:

```typescript title="use-sign-in-wallet.ts"
import { useWalletAccountTransactionSigner } from "@solana/react";
import {
  getBase64EncodedWireTransaction,
  getBase64Encoder,
  getTransactionDecoder,
} from "@solana/kit";

type WalletAccount = Parameters<typeof useWalletAccountTransactionSigner>[0];

/** Signs SDP's base64 transaction in the customer's connected wallet. */
export function useSignInWallet(account: WalletAccount) {
  // Use "solana:mainnet" for a production project.
  const signer = useWalletAccountTransactionSigner(account, "solana:devnet");
  return async (transactionBase64: string): Promise<string> => {
    const unsigned = getTransactionDecoder().decode(getBase64Encoder().encode(transactionBase64));
    // Wallet Standard signers may modify before signing, so check the result below.
    const [signed] = await signer.modifyAndSignTransactions([unsigned]);
    if (!signed) throw new Error("The wallet returned no signed transaction");
    const unchanged =
      signed.messageBytes.length === unsigned.messageBytes.length &&
      signed.messageBytes.every((byte, index) => byte === unsigned.messageBytes[index]);
    if (!unchanged) throw new Error("The wallet changed the transaction; build a new one");
    return getBase64EncodedWireTransaction(signed);
  };
}
```

Send the signed transaction to your backend, which submits it. Some wallets
add instructions before they sign. SDP refuses a changed transaction with
`400`, so check first and ask for a fresh build. Never broadcast it from the
wallet: SDP broadcasts after it records the deposit.
