### How Earn works
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/concepts

> Strategies, positions and shares, who signs, and how each deposit and withdrawal settles.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Earn moves your customer's stablecoins into a strategy and back out again.
This page explains the pieces you work with and the rules that keep balances
honest.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Strategy | A yield source in the catalog: a lending market, a vault, or a yield-bearing token. Each takes one deposit token. |
| Position | One customer wallet's holding in one strategy. |
| Shares | The units a position holds. Withdrawals spend shares, not dollars. |
| Movement | SDP's record of one deposit or withdrawal, from submit to finality. |
| Withdrawal request | SDP's record of a withdrawal that pays out later, through a solver queue or an operator redemption. |
| External wallet | A wallet SDP holds no key for, such as your customer's own wallet. The `/external-wallet/` routes and `ownerAddress` refer to it. |

## Strategies

| Source | Where yield comes from |
| --- | --- |
| DeFi (`sourceKind: "defi"`) | Onchain lending markets and vaults. Returns move with protocol activity. |
| Real-world assets (`sourceKind: "rwa"`) | Tokenized investments backed by assets such as US Treasuries. Returns and redemptions follow the issuer's terms. |

`sourceKind` says where yield comes from, not how a withdrawal settles. Read
each position's [withdrawal options](/docs/earn/withdrawals#1-choose-a-route)
to see which routes it supports. [Strategies](/docs/earn/strategies) covers
the catalog and how to choose.

## Positions and shares

Three amounts describe a position:

| Amount | Field | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shares | `shares` | How much of the strategy the wallet owns, in share units. |
| Share value | `tokenValue` | What those shares are worth now, in the deposit token. |
| Withdrawable shares | `withdrawableShares` | How many shares can leave right now, after locks and liquidity. |

A withdrawal names a share amount, and its payout depends on the strategy's
live state. Quote it with a
[withdrawal preview](/docs/earn/withdrawals#2-withdraw-instantly) instead of
multiplying by an old rate. A missing live value means unavailable, never
zero.

## Who signs

SDP never holds your customer's key. Every deposit and withdrawal follows the
same four steps:

1. Your backend asks SDP to **build** an unsigned transaction.
2. Your customer's wallet **signs** it, without changing or broadcasting it.
3. Your backend **submits** the signed transaction to SDP.
4. SDP verifies it, records a movement, broadcasts it, and tracks it.

Keep your API key on your backend. It can read every position your project
records, so your backend decides which customer may act on which wallet. See
[Embedded Yield](/docs/guides/embedded-yield#authenticate-on-your-backend).

## How a movement settles

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `requested` | SDP recorded the signed transaction and has not seen it onchain yet. |
| `submitted` | SDP broadcast the transaction. |
| `confirmed` | The network confirmed it. Final for display only when settlement is `atomic`. |
| `finalized` | The transaction is final. |
| `failed` | It did not land. `failureReason` says why. |

A movement's `settlement` decides when funds have really moved:

- **`atomic`**: the deposit or withdrawal happens in one transaction. You may
  show it as done at `confirmed` while SDP tracks it to `finalized`.
- **`provider_order`**: the transaction places an order that the provider
  completes later. Confirmation proves the order, not the payout: the
  movement stays `confirmed` until the provider completes it, and only
  `finalized` means it is done.

Withdrawals through a solver queue or an operator redemption also pay out
later. Track them as [withdrawal requests](/docs/earn/withdrawals#track-a-request),
and credit funds only when the payout arrives.

## Where funds go

A vault or lending deposit exchanges the deposit token for shares in the
customer's wallet. A token strategy acquires the yield-bearing token itself.
Either way, the deposited stablecoins go to the protocol or provider, never to
an SDP-owned account.

**warn**

Never send tokens to a strategy's `providerReference`. It identifies the
instrument, not a deposit address. Deposit only through a transaction SDP
builds.

Holding shares in the customer's own wallet does not remove the provider's
custody, liquidity, or withdrawal risks. A position's value can rise or fall
with returns, losses, and fees.

## Sandbox and production

Your API key's project decides the network: a sandbox project runs on devnet
with test tokens, and a production project runs on mainnet with real funds.
The API host and every request stay the same. See
[Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) when you are ready to move.

Next, [make your first deposit](/docs/earn/quickstart) or
[choose a strategy](/docs/earn/strategies).

---

### Strategies
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/strategies

> Find a strategy your project can deposit into, then check its slippage policy, rate, eligibility, and withdrawal terms.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Every deposit names a strategy. List the catalog, keep the strategies your
project can fund, and check each one's terms before you offer it to
customers.

Set `SDP_API_URL` and `SDP_API_KEY` as shown in the
[Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart#before-you-begin).

## List the catalog

[`GET /v1/earn/strategies`](/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-strategies)
returns the strategies your project can see, largest first. It defaults to
your project's cluster: devnet for sandbox, mainnet for production.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/strategies?pageSize=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "strategies": [
      {
        "id": "earn_strategy_3b6a81ce-00b0-4c5a-9761-cb359932e97e",
        "provider": "kamino",
        "providerReference": "C7N2fqV2GvhFghDf5PJSwstyjedjLNCY1cm2Ak7TeU83",
        "name": "Kamino Vault USDC",
        "sourceKind": "defi",
        "depositMints": ["4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU"],
        "shareMint": "CeirL1mAehaM6g2EccgMUQwohNfnuyicskVQ4r9ekXk6",
        "apyType": "variable",
        "liquidityTerm": "instant",
        "status": "active",
        "depositSlippage": null,
        "withdrawalSlippage": null,
        "hostCluster": "devnet",
        "fundable": true
      }
    ],
    "total": 6,
    "page": 1,
    "pageSize": 100
  }
}
```

The catalog pages with `page` and `pageSize` (default 20, up to 100). Keep
reading pages until you have `total` strategies. Narrow the list with
`sourceKind`, `apyType`, or `liquidityTerm`.

## Check that it takes deposits

| Check | Pass when |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `"active"`. Paused and deprecated strategies take no new deposits. |
| `fundable` | `true`. The strategy exists on your project's cluster. |
| `hostCluster` | Matches your project: `devnet` in sandbox, `mainnet-beta` in production. |
| Deposit token | `depositMints[0]` is the token a deposit takes. Fund the wallet with it. |
| Preview | A [deposit preview](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-vault-deposit-preview) returns an empty `blockingIssues`. |

In sandbox, `?cluster=mainnet-beta` lists mainnet strategies for browsing.
They stay `fundable: false`: a sandbox project cannot deposit into them.

Your organization also needs each provider activated, once for all its
projects. Until it is, previews and builds return `403` with `FORBIDDEN` and
`details.reason` set to `provider_not_entitled`:

```json title="Response"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "FORBIDDEN",
    "message": "Kamino requires manual activation for this organization.",
    "details": { "reason": "provider_not_entitled" }
  }
}
```

Ask your SDP contact to activate the provider for your organization.

## Read the slippage policy

`depositSlippage` and `withdrawalSlippage` say whether a transaction needs a
floor derived from a live quote:

| Policy | Deposit | Withdrawal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `null` | Omit `minSharesOut`. | Omit `minAmountOut`. |
| `{ "quoteRequired": true, "defaultToleranceBps": 10 }` | Preview, then send `minSharesOut`. | Preview, then send `minAmountOut`. |

[Slippage floors](/docs/earn/integration-details#slippage-floors) shows how
to compute a floor exactly.

## Show rates and terms

| Field | How to show it |
| --- | --- |
| `currentApy` | A decimal rate: `"0.062"` is 6.2%. When absent, show "Unavailable", never 0%. |
| `apyType` | A `variable` rate moves with the strategy's returns; a `fixed` rate does not. |
| `liquidityTerm` | A label, not a promise. Read live [withdrawal options](/docs/earn/withdrawals#1-choose-a-route) before you offer a withdrawal route. |
| `redemptionDelayDays` | Expected timing, not a guaranteed deadline. |
| `riskMetadata` | Provider fees and risk facts, when the provider reports them. |

An APY describes a rate, not a guaranteed return. Holding a token in the
customer's own wallet does not guarantee principal, backing, or liquidity.

## Confirm eligibility

SDP access authorizes API calls, not investment. For restricted products,
confirm investor, jurisdiction, wallet, subscription, and redemption
requirements with the provider, for each customer and for the wallet that
will hold the position. One usable strategy does not make a provider
permissionless.

## Follow the funds

| Strategy shape | Money in | Money out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vault or lending market | One transaction exchanges the deposit token for shares. | Shares redeem under the provider's liquidity and withdrawal rules. |
| Yield-bearing token | One transaction acquires the token in the customer's wallet. | A sale depends on market liquidity; a redemption may need provider approval. |
| Provider order | A transaction pays into the provider's order. | The provider completes the order later. |

## Paused and deprecated strategies

Pausing or deprecating a strategy stops new deposits only. Existing positions
stay visible and withdrawable, subject to the provider's liquidity. See
[Withdraw funds](/docs/earn/withdrawals).

Next, [make your first deposit](/docs/earn/quickstart).

---

### Deposit funds
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/deposits

> Preview, build, sign, submit, and track a deposit request by request, in cURL or TypeScript.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

A deposit takes six requests and one signature. This page shows each request
and its response, so you can build the flow in any language. For the shortest
path, start with the [Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart).

## Before you begin

You need the Quickstart's setup: `SDP_API_URL` for a beta or experimental
deployment, a sandbox API key with `earn.execute`, a funded test wallet in
`test-wallet.json`, and Node.js for signing. See
[Before you begin](/docs/earn/quickstart#before-you-begin). The cURL examples
also require jq 1.6 or later.

**cURL**

Work in the folder that holds `test-wallet.json`, with `@solana/kit` installed
for the signer:

```bash title="Terminal"
npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install @solana/kit@8
export SDP_API_KEY="sf_..."
export OWNER_ADDRESS="$(solana-keygen pubkey test-wallet.json)"
```

Save this signer as `sign.mjs` in the same folder. It signs SDP's transaction
without changing it and prints the signed transaction:

```javascript title="sign.mjs"
// Sandbox only: signs a base64 transaction with test-wallet.json.
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import {
  createKeyPairFromBytes,
  getBase64EncodedWireTransaction,
  getBase64Encoder,
  getTransactionDecoder,
  partiallySignTransaction,
} from "@solana/kit";

const secretKey = new Uint8Array(JSON.parse(await readFile("test-wallet.json", "utf8")));
const keyPair = await createKeyPairFromBytes(secretKey);
const unsigned = getTransactionDecoder().decode(getBase64Encoder().encode(process.argv[2]));
const signed = await partiallySignTransaction([keyPair], unsigned);
process.stdout.write(getBase64EncodedWireTransaction(signed));
```

**TypeScript**

Use `earn-api.ts` and `test-wallet.ts` from the
[Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart#1-add-the-request-helper).
The steps below are one file, `deposit.ts`, that you run with
`npx tsx deposit.ts`.

## 1. Choose a strategy

List the catalog and keep an active, fundable strategy whose first deposit
mint is devnet USDC and needs no slippage floor.
[Strategies](/docs/earn/strategies) explains each check.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/strategies?pageSize=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" > strategies.json

# The first active, fundable devnet USDC strategy that needs no deposit floor.
STRATEGY_ID="$(jq -er --arg mint "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU" '
  [.data.strategies[] | select(.fundable and .status == "active"
    and .depositSlippage == null and .depositMints[0] == $mint)][0].id
  // error("No devnet USDC strategy is open for deposits")' strategies.json)" || exit 1
export STRATEGY_ID
export AMOUNT="25"  # in the deposit token
echo "$STRATEGY_ID"
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { earnRequest } from "./earn-api";
import { ownerAddress, signWithTestWallet } from "./test-wallet";

type Strategy = {
  id: string;
  status: string;
  fundable: boolean;
  depositMints: string[];
  depositSlippage: unknown;
  withdrawalSlippage: { defaultToleranceBps: number } | null;
};

const { strategies }: { strategies: Strategy[] } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/strategies?pageSize=100",
);
const strategy = strategies.find(
  (s) => s.fundable && s.status === "active" && s.depositSlippage === null
    && s.depositMints[0] === "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
);
if (!strategy) throw new Error("No devnet USDC strategy is open for deposits");
const amount = "25"; // in the deposit token
```

## 2. Preview the deposit

[`POST /v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-vault-deposit-preview)
quotes the shares the deposit would receive right now. It moves nothing.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -nc --arg strategyId "$STRATEGY_ID" --arg amount "$AMOUNT" \
    '{strategyId: $strategyId, amount: $amount}')" > preview.json

jq -e '.data.blockingIssues == []' preview.json || echo "Resolve blockingIssues first" >&2
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const preview = await earnRequest("/v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews", {
  strategyId: strategy.id,
  amount,
});
if (preview.blockingIssues.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(`Preview blocked: ${JSON.stringify(preview.blockingIssues)}`);
}
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "strategyId": "earn_strategy_3b6a81ce-00b0-4c5a-9761-cb359932e97e",
    "sharesOut": "25",
    "shareDecimals": 6,
    "blockingIssues": []
  }
}
```

Resolve every `blockingIssues` entry before you build, even on a `200`. A
preview does not reserve the rate. For a strategy whose `depositSlippage` is
not null, use `sharesOut` to set `minSharesOut`, as
[Slippage floors](/docs/earn/integration-details#slippage-floors) shows.
Ignore the response's `feeSponsored`: it describes Treasury custody-wallet
movements, and your customer's wallet pays its own fees unless you set a
`feePayer`.

## 3. Build the transaction

[`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-deposit-transaction)
returns an unsigned transaction for the customer's wallet.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -nc --arg strategyId "$STRATEGY_ID" --arg ownerAddress "$OWNER_ADDRESS" \
    --arg amount "$AMOUNT" \
    '{strategyId: $strategyId, ownerAddress: $ownerAddress, amount: $amount}')" \
  > build.json
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const { transaction: built } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions",
  { strategyId: strategy.id, ownerAddress, amount },
);
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "transaction": {
      "transactionId": "earn_external_wallet_transaction_b116f3ed-5f19-41b1-85cd-8afe6b37875d",
      "transaction": "AQAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA...",
      "lastValidBlockHeight": "14846",
      "sponsored": false,
      "ownerAddress": "Af89Mkuvo6AcLDbs7Fxs1FPsnnbD9KrY9NfmaFXHqmPo",
      "provider": "kamino",
      "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
      "amount": "25",
      "minSharesOut": null
    }
  }
}
```

Keep `transactionId` and the base64 `transaction` together. The network
accepts the transaction until block height `lastValidBlockHeight`, about a
minute after the build, so sign and submit promptly. The customer's wallet
pays the network fee, plus rent for the accounts a first deposit creates,
unless you name a `feePayer`; see
[Fees and sponsorship](/docs/earn/integration-details#fees-and-sponsorship).

## 4. Sign it

The customer's wallet signs the exact bytes, without changing or broadcasting
them. Here the test wallet stands in. In production, sign in your app, as the
[Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart#sign-in-your-customers-wallet) shows.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
export TRANSACTION_ID="$(jq -r '.data.transaction.transactionId' build.json)"
export SIGNED_TRANSACTION="$(node sign.mjs "$(jq -r '.data.transaction.transaction' build.json)")"
test -n "$SIGNED_TRANSACTION" || echo "Signing failed: is @solana/kit installed here?" >&2
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const signedTransaction = await signWithTestWallet(built.transaction);
```

## 5. Submit it

[`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-deposit)
takes the signed transaction. SDP checks it against the build, records the
deposit, then broadcasts it. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
# Save the idempotency key with the signed body before the first send; retry with both.
export IDEMPOTENCY_KEY="$(node -e 'console.log(crypto.randomUUID())')"
jq -nc --arg transactionId "$TRANSACTION_ID" --arg signedTransaction "$SIGNED_TRANSACTION" \
  '{transactionId: $transactionId, signedTransaction: $signedTransaction}' > submit.json

curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  --data-binary @submit.json > deposit.json
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
// Save the idempotency key with the signed body before the first send; retry with both.
const idempotencyKey = randomUUID();
const { deposit } = await earnRequest(
  "/v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits",
  { transactionId: built.transactionId, signedTransaction },
  idempotencyKey,
);
```

Persist the returned `positionId` with the selected strategy's
`withdrawalSlippage` in your backend's position record. Keep `null` explicitly
when no floor is supported. A strategy can leave the catalog while its
positions remain withdrawable; use this saved policy when building an exit.

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "deposit": {
      "movementId": "earn_movement_505a6c34-f804-4abd-b6a9-315d031bdf1f",
      "positionId": "earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b",
      "direction": "deposit",
      "status": "submitted",
      "settlement": "atomic",
      "signature": "3dhkSPLiQZQPXL96fWzMdWJtdbtAffkBKXw2xhsYbV3VNSnYrVAcdx1czsnLsE1ou4SvLecGdSYe4QpAuZdfjJAf",
      "amount": "25",
      "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
      "tokenAmount": null,
      "replayed": false
    }
  }
}
```

On some strategies a deposit's `tokenAmount` stays null until `finalized`, so
read the deposited amount there. If the response is lost or times out, send
the same body with the same idempotency key.
SDP returns the original deposit, in its current state, with
`replayed: true` instead of depositing twice.
[Retry safely](/docs/earn/integration-details#retry-safely) covers the other
cases.

## 6. Track it to finality

Poll [`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/{movementId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-movement)
until the status is `finalized` or `failed`.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
MOVEMENT_ID="$(jq -r '.data.deposit.movementId' deposit.json)"
# Every second for a minute, then every five seconds, for up to three minutes.
for attempt in $(seq 84); do
  curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/$MOVEMENT_ID" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" > movement.json
  jq -e '.data.movement.status | IN("finalized", "failed")' movement.json >/dev/null && break
  if [ "$attempt" -le 60 ]; then sleep 1; else sleep 5; fi
done
jq '.data.movement | {status, settlement, tokenAmount, failureReason}' movement.json
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
import { waitForMovement } from "./earn-api";

const movement = await waitForMovement(deposit.movementId);
if (movement.status === "failed") throw new Error(movement.failureReason ?? "Deposit failed");
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "movement": {
      "movementId": "earn_movement_505a6c34-f804-4abd-b6a9-315d031bdf1f",
      "direction": "deposit",
      "status": "finalized",
      "settlement": "atomic",
      "amount": "25",
      "tokenAmount": "25",
      "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
      "failureReason": null
    }
  }
}
```

With `settlement: "atomic"`, you may show the deposit as done at `confirmed`
while you keep tracking to `finalized`. A `provider_order` deposit stays
`confirmed` until the provider completes it, so treat it as done only at
`finalized`; see
[How a movement settles](/docs/earn/concepts#how-a-movement-settles).

## 7. Read the position

[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/positions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-external-wallet-positions)
returns the wallet's live positions.

**cURL**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS --get "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "ownerAddress=$OWNER_ADDRESS"
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="deposit.ts (continued)"
const { positions } = await earnRequest(
  `/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions?${new URLSearchParams({ ownerAddress })}`,
);
console.log(JSON.stringify(positions, null, 2));
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "ownerAddress": "Af89Mkuvo6AcLDbs7Fxs1FPsnnbD9KrY9NfmaFXHqmPo",
    "positions": [
      {
        "id": "earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b",
        "label": "Kamino Vault USDC",
        "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
        "shares": "25",
        "withdrawableShares": "25",
        "tokenValue": "25"
      }
    ],
    "hasMore": false,
    "nextCursor": null
  }
}
```

Show a missing `shares` or `tokenValue` as unavailable, never as zero.
[Balances and earnings](/docs/earn/balances) covers earnings, history, and
pagination.

## Errors

| Status | Code | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `BAD_REQUEST` | The submit has no `Idempotency-Key`, or the signed transaction differs from the build, or a signature is missing or invalid. | Send a key. Otherwise build again and sign the exact bytes. |
| `403` | `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` | The API key lacks the grant the route needs, named in `details.action`. | Use an API key with `earn.execute`. |
| `403` | `FORBIDDEN` | `details.reason` is `provider_not_entitled`: your organization is not activated for the provider. | Ask your SDP contact to activate it. |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | SDP has no build with that `transactionId`. | Check the ID, or build again. |
| `409` | `CONFLICT` | The idempotency key was already used for a different build, or the same build arrives under a new idempotency key. | Retry with the original build and idempotency key. Use a new idempotency key only for a new deposit. |

These codes replace the ones on the shared
[Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency) page; see
[Retry safely](/docs/earn/integration-details#retry-safely).

Next, [withdraw funds](/docs/earn/withdrawals) or
[ship Embedded Yield](/docs/guides/embedded-yield).

---

### Balances and earnings
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/balances

> Show each customer's live positions, movement history, and exact earnings, and never show a missing value as zero.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Read balances from live positions and history from recorded movements. Each
per-wallet read takes the customer's wallet as `ownerAddress`, so your
backend decides which wallet a signed-in customer may see. The examples read
it from `OWNER_ADDRESS`, as in [Deposit funds](/docs/earn/deposits#before-you-begin).

Set `SDP_API_URL` and `SDP_API_KEY` as shown in the
[Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart#before-you-begin).

## Positions

[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/positions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-external-wallet-positions)
returns the wallet's live positions.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS --get "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "ownerAddress=$OWNER_ADDRESS"
```

| Field | Show it as |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The position ID. Withdrawals name it. |
| `label` | The strategy's display name. |
| `shares` | The wallet's live share balance. |
| `withdrawableShares` | The shares that can leave right now. |
| `tokenValue` | The live value in the deposit token (`tokenMint`). Every Earn deposit token is a USD stablecoin, so at par this reads as dollars. |
| `unlockTimestamp` | When locked shares become withdrawable, in Unix seconds. Null or absent when nothing is locked. |

Positions come newest first, and repeat deposits into one strategy add to the
same position.

- **A missing live value is unavailable.** When the provider read fails,
  `shares`, `withdrawableShares`, and `tokenValue` are left out. Show
  "Unavailable" and disable withdrawals until a fresh read succeeds. Never
  show zero or an old quote.
- **A wallet with no positions returns an empty list,** not `404`. A fully
  withdrawn position drops out of the list.
- **An open withdrawal request holds shares outside the position.** They
  leave `shares` and `tokenValue` until the request pays out or is canceled,
  so show its `quotedAssets` as an expected payout.
- **`parIntermediate`** appears while the wallet holds an operator
  redemption's intermediate token outside an open request. It keeps the
  position open and counts toward earnings' `currentValue`. See
  [Operator redemptions](/docs/earn/withdrawals#operator-redemptions).

## Movements

Each deposit and withdrawal is a movement. Read one with
[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/{movementId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-movement),
or list a wallet's history, newest first, with
[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements`](/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-external-wallet-movements).

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS --get "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/movements" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "ownerAddress=$OWNER_ADDRESS"
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "ownerAddress": "HM4yQMRMc3gd6TwgraU7r4f4zpJRZmDomzkSPDWmmfi8",
    "movements": [
      {
        "movementId": "earn_movement_a6aed3f5-4f89-4dc6-9d4b-0864021bd80d",
        "direction": "deposit",
        "status": "finalized",
        "settlement": "atomic",
        "amount": "25",
        "denomination": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
        "tokenAmount": "25",
        "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
        "createdAt": "2026-11-06T18:17:55.220Z",
        "confirmedAt": "2026-11-06T18:17:55.374Z",
        "settledAt": "2026-11-06T18:17:58.425Z"
      }
    ],
    "hasMore": false,
    "nextCursor": null
  }
}
```

Show `tokenAmount` in `tokenMint` units for both directions. On a withdrawal,
`amount` is the share quantity, not the payout, and `tokenAmount` stays null
until SDP observes the payout. `confirmedAt` is when the network confirmed
the movement, and `settledAt` is when it finalized. Label requested amounts
and expected queue payouts as such.
[How a movement settles](/docs/earn/concepts#how-a-movement-settles) explains
each status and `settlement`.

## Earnings

[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/earnings`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-earnings)
returns the wallet's balance and earnings for each deposit token.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS --get "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/earnings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "ownerAddress=$OWNER_ADDRESS"
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "earnings": {
      "ownerAddress": "HM4yQMRMc3gd6TwgraU7r4f4zpJRZmDomzkSPDWmmfi8",
      "positionCount": 1,
      "unavailablePositionCount": 0,
      "totalsByToken": [
        {
          "tokenMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
          "currentValue": "25",
          "totalDeposited": "25",
          "totalWithdrawn": "0",
          "earned": "0"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

`currentValue` is the sum of the positions' `tokenValue`, plus any
intermediate tokens. `earned` is
`currentValue + totalWithdrawn - totalDeposited`, and it appears only when it
is exact. It can be negative: right after a deposit, the strategy's share
rounding can leave it slightly below zero. When it is left out,
`earnedUnavailableReason` says why:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `live_value_unavailable` | A position's live value could not be read. |
| `movements_pending` | A deposit or withdrawal is still settling. |
| `withdrawals_pending` | An open withdrawal request holds shares that have not paid out yet. |
| `deposits_not_valued` | SDP did not observe a finalized deposit's amount. |
| `withdrawals_not_valued` | SDP did not observe a finalized withdrawal's payout. |

Show a dash, never `$0`, while `earned` is missing. Three limits apply:

- **Only held positions count.** A fully withdrawn position drops out of
  earnings but stays in the movement history.
- **Outside transfers count.** The live value reads the wallet's whole balance
  in the strategy, including shares acquired outside SDP, while deposits and
  withdrawals come only from SDP's records.
- **It is not an accounting ledger.** It gives no lifetime realized returns or
  daily accrual history. Reconcile against your own records for statements.

## Position totals

[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/positions/summary`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-position-summary)
returns live totals across every customer wallet in your project, by token and
by strategy. It takes no `ownerAddress`.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions/summary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

Wallet addresses are personal data, so they are left out unless you pass
`includeOwnerAddresses=true`. Add `includePositions=true` to also get each
wallet's positions; it requires the address opt-in, or the request returns
`400`.

Never send this summary, or your API key, to a customer's browser.

## Paginate every list

| List | Paging |
| --- | --- |
| Strategies | `page` and `pageSize` (default 20, up to 100), until you have `total`. |
| Positions, movements, withdrawal requests | `limit` (default 20, up to 100) and `before`, set to the previous page's `nextCursor`, until `hasMore` is `false`. |

Treat a missing or repeated cursor as an error: a silently short list hides a
customer's money. Earn lists differ from the shared
[Pagination](/docs/reference/conventions/pagination) conventions: the catalog
returns `total`, `page`, and `pageSize` inside `data`, and the cursor lists
take their cursor as `before`.

---

### Withdraw funds
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/withdrawals

> Choose a live withdrawal route, withdraw instantly or by request, and confirm the payout reached the customer's wallet.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

A withdrawal spends shares from a position and pays the deposit token back to
the wallet that owns it. Some routes pay in the same transaction; others pay
later. Read the live routes first, then follow the one your customer chooses.

Set `SDP_API_URL` and `SDP_API_KEY` as shown in the
[Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart#before-you-begin).

## 1. Choose a route

[`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-options`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-options)
reads each route from live provider state.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl --fail-with-body -sS "${SDP_API_URL:?Set SDP_API_URL}/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-options" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"positionId": "earn_position_0432ffeb-c574-4b11-80dc-a09defb68fcc"}'
```

```json title="Response (trimmed)"
{
  "data": {
    "positionId": "earn_position_0432ffeb-c574-4b11-80dc-a09defb68fcc",
    "instant": true,
    "providerOrder": false,
    "queued": true,
    "queueAsset": {
      "assetMint": "4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU",
      "allowWithdrawals": true,
      "secondsToMaturity": 3600,
      "minimumSecondsToDeadline": 60,
      "maximumSecondsToDeadline": 7776000,
      "minimumDiscountBps": 0,
      "maximumDiscountBps": 100,
      "minimumShares": "0.000001",
      "shareDecimals": 6
    },
    "parRedemption": null
  }
}
```

| Route | When it is offered | Pays out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instant withdrawal | `instant: true` | In the same transaction. |
| Provider order | `providerOrder: true` | Later, when the provider completes the order. |
| Solver queue | `queued: true`, with live terms in `queueAsset` | Later, at a discount, when a solver fulfills the request. |
| Operator redemption | `parRedemption` is present | Later, at par, when the operator settles the request. |

A position offers an instant withdrawal or a provider order, never both, and
the same withdrawal endpoints build whichever it offers. When more than one
route is offered, let your customer choose, and keep their choice. Never infer
a route from the strategy's `liquidityTerm`. A failed read or missing terms
means the route is unavailable, not that it pays zero.

## 2. Withdraw instantly

An instant withdrawal works like a deposit: preview, build, sign, submit, and
track. Withdraw at most the position's live `withdrawableShares`: a preview
does not check the wallet's balance.

| Step | Request |
| --- | --- |
| Preview | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-previews`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-preview) |
| Build | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-transaction) |
| Submit | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawals`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal), with an `Idempotency-Key` |
| Track | [`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/{movementId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-movement) |

The example uses the Quickstart's `earn-api.ts` and `test-wallet.ts`, and
`floor.ts` from [Slippage floors](/docs/earn/integration-details#slippage-floors).
Call `withdraw` with the `positionId` and `withdrawalSlippage` saved in your
backend after the deposit, plus the share amount your customer chose:

```typescript title="withdraw.ts"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { earnRequest, waitForMovement } from "./earn-api";
import { floorForTolerance } from "./floor";
import { ownerAddress, signWithTestWallet } from "./test-wallet";

type SavedPosition = {
  positionId: string;
  withdrawalSlippage: { defaultToleranceBps: number } | null;
};
type Position = { id: string; withdrawableShares?: string };

export async function withdraw(savedPosition: SavedPosition, shares: string) {
  let position: Position | undefined;
  let before: string | null = null;
  do {
    const query = new URLSearchParams({ ownerAddress, limit: "100" });
    if (before !== null) query.set("before", before);
    const page: { positions: Position[]; nextCursor: string | null } = await earnRequest(
      `/v1/earn/external-wallet/positions?${query}`,
    );
    position = page.positions.find((p) => p.id === savedPosition.positionId);
    before = page.nextCursor;
  } while (!position && before !== null);
  if (!position || position.withdrawableShares === undefined) {
    throw new Error("The saved position cannot withdraw right now");
  }

  const preview = await earnRequest("/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-previews", {
    positionId: position.id,
    shares,
  });
  if (preview.blockingIssues.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(`Preview blocked: ${JSON.stringify(preview.blockingIssues)}`);
  }

  // Send a floor only when the saved policy takes one; never require a catalog listing to exit.
  const policy = savedPosition.withdrawalSlippage;
  const minAmountOut = policy
    ? floorForTolerance(preview.assetsOut, preview.assetDecimals, policy.defaultToleranceBps)
    : undefined;

  const { transaction: built } = await earnRequest(
    "/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-transactions",
    { positionId: position.id, shares, minAmountOut },
  );
  const signedTransaction = await signWithTestWallet(built.transaction);

  const { withdrawal } = await earnRequest(
    "/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawals",
    { transactionId: built.transactionId, signedTransaction },
    randomUUID(),
  );
  return waitForMovement(withdrawal.movementId);
}
```

```json title="Preview response"
{
  "data": {
    "positionId": "earn_position_e3053c7b-e41e-4f21-b4dc-e229ab95f40b",
    "assetsOut": "10",
    "assetDecimals": 6,
    "blockingIssues": []
  }
}
```

The preview quotes the payout; it does not reserve it. The build requires
`minAmountOut` when the strategy's `withdrawalSlippage` is not null, and
refuses it when the policy is null. The position supplies the vault and mints,
so a delisted strategy stays exitable. Keep the deposit-time policy with the
position; do not require the strategy to appear in today's catalog.

If the build reports that the floor policy changed, refresh the policy with
your SDP contact before retrying. Never guess a policy from a missing catalog
row.

At `finalized`, `tokenAmount` is the payout SDP observed. Check the customer's
token balance onchain if you need independent proof, then refresh
[balances](/docs/earn/balances).

## Provider orders

A provider order takes an exact share amount and pays out after the provider
prices and settles it. Its preview may return `501`, which does not block the
build. No floor can bound a later price, so omit `minAmountOut` when the
policy is null.

The withdrawal's `settlement` is `provider_order`. Confirmation proves the
order transaction, not the payout: the movement stays `confirmed` until the
provider completes the order. Show it as pending until it reaches `finalized`;
see [How a movement settles](/docs/earn/concepts#how-a-movement-settles).

## Asynchronous withdrawals

A solver queue or an operator redemption creates a withdrawal request. The
request transaction moves shares, never the payout, so track the request until
it pays out or is canceled.

### Solver queues

The request escrows shares. After `secondsToMaturity`, a solver may fulfill it
at the agreed discount until the deadline. Before the customer confirms, show
the live terms from `queueAsset`: minimum shares, the discount range, maturity,
and the deadline range.

Send `shares`, `discountBps`, and `deadlineSeconds`, each inside the live
terms; `mechanism` defaults to `solverQueue`. The deadline counts from
maturity, not from creation, and both run on the cluster's clock:
`maturityTimestamp` and `deadlineTimestamp` are onchain Unix times.

- **The discount is your customer's cost.** A larger `discountBps` makes a
  solver more likely to fill the request, and the customer receives that much
  less.
- **The deadline is how long solvers have.** A longer `deadlineSeconds` gives
  them more time, but keeps the shares escrowed longer if none fills it.
- **Open requests leave the balance.** Escrowed shares drop out of the
  position's `shares` and earnings' `currentValue`, and earnings report
  `withdrawals_pending`. Show the request's `quotedAssets` as an expected
  payout.

### Operator redemptions

The request converts shares into an intermediate token and authorizes the
operator to settle it for the deposit token at par. Read the live
`parRedemption` terms: minimum shares, `intermediateMint`, `assetMint`, and
whether cancellation is allowed.

Send `mechanism: "operatorRedemption"` with either `shares` or
`intermediateAmount` from an existing `parIntermediate` holding, never both.
A null `minimumShares` means the conversion rate is unavailable: the preview
reports a blocking issue.

### Create a request

| Step | Request |
| --- | --- |
| Preview | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/queued-withdrawal-previews`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-queued-withdrawal-preview) |
| Build | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-transaction) |
| Submit | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request), with an `Idempotency-Key` |

Resolve every `blockingIssues` entry in the preview, then build, sign, and
submit as for an instant withdrawal. Save the returned `withdrawalRequestId`.

Keep the signed request and its idempotency key until the request resolves.
The wallet may already have broadcast it, so SDP accepts it even after its
build expires:

| Submit answer | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `409 CONFLICT` on a late request | SDP released the build's reservation and accepts the request once the exact transaction is finalized. Retry the same bytes and key. For an operator redemption whose cycle already closed, contact support instead. |
| `400 TRANSACTION_FAILED` | The transaction finalized as failed. Build a new request. |
| `503` | SDP could not finish checking the request's history. Retry the same bytes and key, and contact support if it persists. |

### Track a request

Poll [`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests/{withdrawalRequestId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request)
every minute or two. Status values spell it `cancelled`.

| Status | Meaning | What to show |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `creating` | SDP recorded the signed request; its chain outcome is unresolved. | Pending. |
| `pending` | Waiting for maturity or for the operator. | Pending, with the expected timing. |
| `fulfillable` | A solver may fulfill it now. | Pending. |
| `expiredCancelable` | The solver deadline passed without fulfillment. | Offer cancellation. |
| `cancelling` | A cancellation was submitted; a fulfillment can still race it. | Canceling. |
| `closedOrUnknown` | The request closed, and SDP has not yet proved a payout or a cancellation. | Pending; keep tracking. |
| `fulfilled` | SDP observed the payout. `assetsPaid` holds the amount. | Done. |
| `cancelled` | SDP observed the cancellation. | Canceled; refresh holdings. |
| `failed` | It did not happen: SDP decides that only after repeated checks find no trace of it. `failureReason` says why. | Failed. |

Only `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, and `failed` are final, and only `fulfilled`
pays out. Never credit `quotedAssets`, a request transaction, or a
cancellation as received funds. A solver queue request that no solver takes
stays `fulfillable` until its deadline, then becomes `expiredCancelable`, and
its shares stay escrowed until the customer cancels it.

On startup and after reconnecting, restore every open request:
[`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests?ownerAddress=<wallet>&settled=false`](/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-requests),
reading every page.

**warn**

Sign withdrawal requests and cancellations without broadcasting them, and
submit them through SDP promptly. If a wallet broadcasts one itself and SDP
first sees it after the build expires, SDP may not be able to track it.

### Cancel a request

Offer cancellation for a solver queue request only at `expiredCancelable`,
never from a client clock; building one earlier returns `409 CONFLICT`. An
operator redemption can be canceled while `pending` if its live terms allow
it. Refresh the request first: a fulfillment can race the cancellation.

| Step | Request |
| --- | --- |
| Build | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancel-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancel-transaction) |
| Submit | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancellations`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancellation) |

Both steps take `earn.manage`, and cancellation stays available after
production access is removed or new deposits are disabled. Use a new
`Idempotency-Key` for the cancellation. A canceled solver request returns
the escrowed shares; a canceled operator redemption leaves the intermediate
token, not the original shares. Refresh holdings before another withdrawal.

---

## Earn: Integrate

### Embedded Yield
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/embedded-yield

> Build customer-signed deposits, balances, and withdrawals into your app, from first request to go-live.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

Embedded Yield lets your customers earn from their own wallets inside your
app. Your backend calls SDP with your API key, your app asks the customer's
wallet to sign, and SDP verifies, broadcasts, and tracks every movement. SDP
never holds the customer's key.

New to Earn? Run the [Quickstart](/docs/earn/quickstart) first, then come
back to build the full integration.

## How the pieces fit

| Part | Does | Never |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your backend | Holds the API key. Previews, builds, submits, and reads. Decides which customer may use which wallet. | Sends the API key to a browser or mobile app. |
| Your app | Shows quotes and status. Asks the customer's wallet to sign. | Broadcasts the transaction. |
| The customer's wallet | Signs the exact transaction SDP built. Owns the position and receives payouts. | Shares its private key. |
| SDP | Builds each transaction, verifies the signatures, records the movement, broadcasts it, and tracks it to finality. | Holds the customer's key or pools their funds. |

A deposit then runs: your backend builds, your app collects the signature,
your backend submits, and your app shows the result as your backend tracks
it.

## Authenticate on your backend

Create an API key in each project with the grants your integration uses:

| Grant | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `earn.read` | Strategies, previews, positions, movements, earnings, and withdrawal requests. |
| `earn.execute` | Builds and submits for deposits, withdrawals, and withdrawal requests. Includes `earn.read`. |
| `earn.manage` | Building and submitting a withdrawal request cancellation. Includes `earn.read`. |

`earn.execute` and `earn.manage` do not include each other. The backend
module reads one `SDP_API_KEY`, so give that key every grant you call through
it. See [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys).

Withdrawals and cancellations stay available after production access is
removed or new deposits are disabled. A suspended organization still cannot
authenticate, and Earn runs only on deployments whose release channel
includes it.

Your API key can read every customer wallet your project has recorded. Before
any request, check that the signed-in customer owns the `ownerAddress` you
send, for example by verifying a message the wallet signed when the customer
linked it. Custody-wallet scopes on the API key do not apply to customer wallets:
the customer's signature authorizes each transaction.

## Get the backend module

The dashboard generates a TypeScript module for a strategy with every call
this guide uses:

1. In the dashboard, open **Markets** > **Embedded Yield** > **Integrate**.
2. Choose a strategy. Only fundable strategies can be selected.
3. Click **Copy all code**, and save it as a server-only file such as
   `earn.ts`. Set `SDP_API_KEY` in your backend's environment.

The module holds the strategy ID and the API URL for the project you
generated it in, so generate it again for production. It needs Node.js 20.18
or later, and `@solana/kit` only for its fee sponsor signer.

| Task | Module function |
| --- | --- |
| List the catalog | `listEarnStrategies` |
| Quote a deposit | `previewEarnDeposit` |
| Build a deposit | `buildEarnDepositTransaction` |
| Collect signatures | `signEarnTransaction`, `createSponsorSigner` |
| Submit a deposit | `submitEarnDeposit` |
| Track a movement | `waitForEarnMovement`, `getEarnMovement` |
| Read balances | `listEarnPositions` (every page), `getEarnEarnings`, `listEarnMovements` (one page per call) |
| Withdraw instantly | `previewEarnWithdrawal`, `buildEarnWithdrawalTransaction`, `submitEarnWithdrawal` |
| Choose a route | `getEarnWithdrawalOptions` |
| Request a withdrawal | `previewEarnQueuedWithdrawal`, `previewEarnParRedemption`, `buildEarnQueuedWithdrawalRequest`, `buildEarnParRedemptionRequest`, `submitEarnWithdrawalRequest` |
| Track requests | `getEarnWithdrawalRequest`, `waitForEarnQueuedWithdrawal`, `listPendingEarnQueuedWithdrawals` |
| Cancel a request | `buildEarnWithdrawalRequestCancellation`, `submitEarnWithdrawalRequestCancellation` |

When SDP refuses a request, a module function throws an `EarnApiError` with
`status`, `code`, `details`, and `retryAfter`. Branch on those, never on the
message.

Prefer raw requests? Every function maps to one endpoint in
[Deposit funds](/docs/earn/deposits) and
[Withdraw funds](/docs/earn/withdrawals).

## Make a deposit

| Step | Module function | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Quote | `previewEarnDeposit` | [`POST /v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-vault-deposit-preview) |
| 2. Build | `buildEarnDepositTransaction` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-deposit-transaction) |
| 3. Sign | `signEarnTransaction` | In the customer's wallet |
| 4. Submit | `submitEarnDeposit` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-deposit) |
| 5. Track | `waitForEarnMovement` | [`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/{movementId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-movement) |

`buildEarnDepositTransaction` previews the deposit itself when the strategy
needs a floor; call `previewEarnDeposit` too when you want to show your
customer a quote first.

`signEarnTransaction(built, customerSigner, sponsorSigner?)` passes the
base64 transaction to your signer, checks that the signed message is
unchanged, and adds your sponsor's signature when the build named a
`feePayer`. `createSponsorSigner(secretKey, feePayerAddress)` makes that
sponsor signer from your fee payer's 64-byte secret key, the array a Solana
CLI keypair file holds. The Quickstart shows a
[customer signer for a browser wallet](/docs/earn/quickstart#sign-in-your-customers-wallet).

Three rules keep deposits safe:

- **Sign exactly what SDP built.** The wallet must not change or broadcast
  the transaction. SDP refuses a changed one with `400`.
- **Save before you submit.** Store the idempotency key with the signed
  transaction, then submit. After an uncertain response, retry with both
  unchanged; see [Retry safely](/docs/earn/integration-details#retry-safely).
- **Track to the end.** Save `movementId` and track it until `finalized` or
  `failed`.

## Show balances

Read positions for withdrawals, earnings for the totals your customer sees,
and movements for their history. [Balances and earnings](/docs/earn/balances)
covers every field. Two rules matter most:

- Show a missing live value as unavailable, never as zero.
- Read every page of a list. A short list hides money.

## Withdraw

1. Read the position's live `withdrawableShares` with `listEarnPositions`,
   then its routes with `getEarnWithdrawalOptions`.
2. For an instant withdrawal, preview, build, sign, submit, and track, as for
   a deposit.
3. For a solver queue or operator redemption, create a withdrawal request and
   track it to `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, or `failed`.
4. On startup, restore every open request with
   `listPendingEarnQueuedWithdrawals`.

| Step | Module function | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose a route | `getEarnWithdrawalOptions` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-options`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-options) |
| Withdraw instantly | `buildEarnWithdrawalTransaction`, `submitEarnWithdrawal` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-transaction), [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawals`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal) |
| Preview a request | `previewEarnQueuedWithdrawal` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/queued-withdrawal-previews`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-queued-withdrawal-preview) |
| Build a request | `buildEarnQueuedWithdrawalRequest` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-transaction) |
| Submit a request | `submitEarnWithdrawalRequest` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request) |
| Track a request | `getEarnWithdrawalRequest` | [`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests/{withdrawalRequestId}`](/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request) |
| Cancel a request | `buildEarnWithdrawalRequestCancellation`, `submitEarnWithdrawalRequestCancellation` | [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancel-transactions`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancel-transaction), [`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancellations`](/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancellation) |

A withdrawal spends shares, not a dollar amount, and a request transaction
is not a payout. [Withdraw funds](/docs/earn/withdrawals) covers each route.

## Go live

- [ ] Get production access: request mainnet access and switch to your
      production project, as steps 1 and 2 of
      [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) show. Embedded Yield needs
      no custody provider or wallet funding.
- [ ] Create a production API key with your Earn grants, and regenerate the
      backend module in your production project. Strategy IDs differ per
      environment.
- [ ] Sign with your customer's wallet on `solana:mainnet`.
- [ ] Support deposit floors. Nearly every production deposit requires
      `minSharesOut`. The module sets it from a live preview when the
      strategy's `depositSlippage` asked for one at generation, so regenerate
      it if a build starts requiring a floor.
- [ ] Persist idempotency keys and signed transactions before you submit.
- [ ] Restore open work after every restart: keep tracking each saved
      `movementId` that is not `finalized` or `failed`, and restore open
      requests with `listPendingEarnQueuedWithdrawals`.
- [ ] Confirm investor and wallet eligibility for each strategy you offer;
      see [Strategies](/docs/earn/strategies#confirm-eligibility).
- [ ] Decide who pays fees, and if you sponsor them, bound and monitor your
      fee payer; see [Fees and sponsorship](/docs/earn/integration-details#fees-and-sponsorship).

### Integration details
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/earn/integration-details

> Slippage floors, fees and sponsorship, swap-funded deposits, retries, errors, and polling for a production Earn integration.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

These rules apply to every Earn integration. Read them before you take real
deposits.

## Slippage floors

A floor is the least a transaction may return: `minSharesOut` on a deposit,
`minAmountOut` on a withdrawal. A strategy's `depositSlippage` and
`withdrawalSlippage` say whether it takes one, as
[Read the slippage policy](/docs/earn/strategies#read-the-slippage-policy)
shows. When a policy is not null, preview first and send the floor: the build
refuses the transaction without it.

A null policy means the transaction cannot enforce a floor: a provider order
is priced later, and some sandbox vaults lack the floor instruction. Omit the
floor then, because a build refuses one it cannot enforce. In production,
nearly every deposit takes a floor. A preview quotes the rate; it does not
reserve it.

Compute the floor in integer base units, never with a JavaScript `number`:

```typescript title="floor.ts"
/** Takes `toleranceBps` off a decimal quote, rounding down to the mint's scale. */
export function floorForTolerance(quote: string, decimals: number, toleranceBps: number): string {
  if (!Number.isInteger(toleranceBps) || toleranceBps < 1 || toleranceBps > 1_000) {
    throw new Error("Tolerance must be 1 to 1,000 basis points");
  }
  const [whole = "", fraction = ""] = quote.split(".");
  const significant = fraction.replace(/0+$/, "");
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(whole) || !/^\d*$/.test(fraction) || significant.length > decimals) {
    throw new Error("The quote is not a decimal at the mint's scale");
  }
  const units = BigInt(whole + significant.padEnd(decimals, "0"));
  if (units === 0n) throw new Error("The quote is zero");
  const floored = (units * BigInt(10_000 - toleranceBps)) / 10_000n || 1n;
  const digits = floored.toString().padStart(decimals + 1, "0");
  if (decimals === 0) return digits;
  const fractionPart = digits.slice(-decimals).replace(/0+$/, "");
  return fractionPart ? `${digits.slice(0, -decimals)}.${fractionPart}` : digits.slice(0, -decimals);
}

// floorForTolerance("50", 6, 10) returns "49.95": a 10 bps floor on 50 shares.
```

Use the preview's `shareDecimals` for a deposit floor and `assetDecimals` for
a withdrawal floor. Start from the policy's `defaultToleranceBps`, and let
your customer choose another; this helper accepts 1 to 1,000 basis points.
The [backend module](/docs/guides/embedded-yield#get-the-backend-module)
ships the same function whenever its strategy needs a floor.

## Fees and sponsorship

By default the customer's wallet pays each transaction's network fee and the
rent for any account it creates:

| Transaction | Accounts it can create |
| --- | --- |
| A first deposit into a strategy | The share account, about 0.002 SOL. Some providers also create an account for the wallet, for up to about 0.0035 SOL in all. |
| A withdrawal request | The request's own accounts, about 0.0027 SOL. |

Rent is separate from the deposit and its yield, and it is not part of
`earned`. Where a request's rent goes when it closes depends on the provider's
program; Hastra returns it to the owner. To pay these costs for your
customer, sponsor the transaction:

1. Set `feePayer` to a wallet your backend controls when you build.
2. Have the customer's wallet sign first.
3. Check that the message is unchanged and that its fee payer is your wallet,
   then add your signature to the same transaction.
4. Submit the transaction with both signatures.

With raw requests, run step 3 on your backend with your fee payer's key pair:

```typescript title="sponsor.ts"
import {
  getAddressFromPublicKey,
  getBase64EncodedWireTransaction,
  getBase64Encoder,
  getCompiledTransactionMessageDecoder,
  getTransactionDecoder,
  partiallySignTransaction,
} from "@solana/kit";

const decode = (base64: string) =>
  getTransactionDecoder().decode(getBase64Encoder().encode(base64));

/** Adds your fee payer's signature to a transaction the customer's wallet signed. */
export async function cosignAsFeePayer(
  unsignedBase64: string,
  customerSignedBase64: string,
  feePayer: CryptoKeyPair,
): Promise<string> {
  const unsigned = decode(unsignedBase64);
  const signed = decode(customerSignedBase64);
  const unchanged =
    signed.messageBytes.length === unsigned.messageBytes.length &&
    signed.messageBytes.every((byte, index) => byte === unsigned.messageBytes[index]);
  if (!unchanged) throw new Error("The wallet changed the transaction; build a new one");

  // The fee payer is the message's first account.
  const { staticAccounts } = getCompiledTransactionMessageDecoder().decode(signed.messageBytes);
  if (staticAccounts[0] !== (await getAddressFromPublicKey(feePayer.publicKey))) {
    throw new Error("This build's fee payer is not your wallet");
  }
  return getBase64EncodedWireTransaction(await partiallySignTransaction([feePayer], signed));
}
```

Pass it the build's `transaction` and the customer's signed transaction, then
submit what it returns. A missing sponsor signature fails the submit with
`400`, and changing the fee payer means a new build and new signatures. The
build's `sponsored` field stays `false`: it reports whether SDP paid, and SDP
never pays for an external wallet. In the
[backend module](/docs/guides/embedded-yield#get-the-backend-module),
`signEarnTransaction` runs steps 2 and 3, and `createSponsorSigner` checks
the fee payer before it signs.

- Sponsor only builds your backend started for an authenticated customer.
- Keep your sponsor's SOL balance small, rate-limit sponsored requests, and
  watch the spend.
- Store the sponsor's key in your secret manager.

The catalog's `feeSponsored` describes deposits and withdrawals from a Treasury custody
wallet. It never applies to a customer's wallet.

A full withdrawal from a Kamino strategy leaves the empty share account open.
The customer's wallet can close it to recover the rent; do not promise an
automatic refund.

## Swap-funded deposits

Set `sourceTokenMint` to fund a deposit with a different supported
stablecoin. SDP adds a Jupiter swap to the deposit's deposit token in the
same transaction, so both happen or neither does. Swap routes need mainnet,
so you cannot test them in sandbox.

When the two do not fit in one transaction, the build returns
`requiresSeparateSwap: true` with a `swap` and a `followUp` instead of
`transaction`:

1. Save the swap's signed bytes, its signature, and the follow-up body.
2. Broadcast the swap yourself and confirm it.
3. Build the follow-up deposit with its original floor and fee payer.

SDP does not record the standalone swap as a movement, so your app owns its
recovery. Resolve an unfinished swap before you start another.

## Retry safely

Every Earn submit takes an `Idempotency-Key`. Use a new random UUID for each
new deposit, withdrawal, request, or cancellation, and save it with the
signed transaction before the first send. Never put customer data in an
idempotency key.

| Situation | What SDP does | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A submit times out or returns `5xx`. | Nothing twice. | Retry with the same idempotency key and body. |
| You retry with the same idempotency key and `transactionId`. | Returns the original movement in its current state, with `replayed: true`, even if the signed bytes differ. | Track it as usual. |
| You reuse an idempotency key for a different build. | `409 CONFLICT`. Nothing runs. | Retry the original build, or use a new idempotency key for a new action. |
| You submit the same build under a new idempotency key. | `409 CONFLICT`. | Find the original action and its idempotency key. |
| The blockhash expired before you submitted. | Records the original signed bytes, which may already have landed. If they never did, the movement ends `failed` with `Transaction blockhash expired before confirmation`. | Submit the original and track it. Do not rebuild until it fails. |
| A late withdrawal request returns `409 CONFLICT`. | Waits to see the exact signed transaction finalized. | Retry the same bytes and key. |
| Recovery finds the transaction finalized as failed. | `400 TRANSACTION_FAILED`. Nothing moved. | Build a new transaction. |
| An unsigned build expired. | Nothing has moved. | Build again before asking for a signature. |
| The preview has blocking issues. | Nothing has moved. | Resolve them and preview again. |

Earn's submits keep their own idempotency rules, which replace the shared
[Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency) page's. A submit without
a key returns `400 BAD_REQUEST`, and a misused key returns `409 CONFLICT`,
never `422`. A key stays bound to its movement for good, with no 24-hour
window, so never reuse one for a new action.

Submit withdrawal requests and cancellations through SDP promptly. If a
wallet broadcasts one itself and SDP first sees it after its build expires,
SDP may be unable to track it. Keep unresolved actions visible, and never
assume no funds moved.

## Errors

Every error has the shape `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`.
The codes Earn integrations meet most:

| Status | Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `BAD_REQUEST` | A field is invalid, the `Idempotency-Key` is missing, or the signed transaction differs from the build. | Read `message` and `details`, fix the request, and build again when the transaction changed. |
| `400` | `TRANSACTION_FAILED` | Recovery found the submitted transaction finalized as failed. | Build a new transaction. |
| `403` | `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` | The API key lacks the grant in `details.action`. | Add the grant to the API key. |
| `403` | `FORBIDDEN` | `details.reason` is `provider_not_entitled`: your organization is not activated for the provider. With `provider_not_offered`, SDP takes no new deposits for it. | Ask your SDP contact to activate it. Withdrawals still work either way. |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | No such strategy, position, movement, build, or request in your project. | Check the ID and the project. |
| `409` | `CONFLICT` | An idempotency key or a signed transaction was already used differently, a late withdrawal request awaits proof that it landed, or a request cannot be canceled yet. | See [Retry safely](#retry-safely). Retry a late request with its exact bytes and key; for a cancellation, wait for `expiredCancelable`. |
| `429` | `RATE_LIMITED` | You are over your rate limit. | Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry. |
| `501` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | The provider cannot quote this operation. | Continue without the preview when the floor policy is null. |
| `503` | `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | SDP could not read the provider's live state or reach a dependency. | Retry with backoff, and show the action as unavailable meanwhile. Retry a submit with the same idempotency key and body. |

See [Errors](/docs/reference/conventions/errors) for the shared error model.

## Poll politely

Track a movement by polling its `GET` route about once a second for the
first minute, then every five seconds. Stop at `finalized` or `failed`, and
treat `429` as a signal to slow down. Withdrawal requests can take hours or
days, so poll them every minute or two, and restore them on startup instead
of holding a loop open. The backend module's wait functions follow this
schedule. See
[Rate limits](/docs/reference/conventions/rate-limits).

### Self-hosting
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/self-hosting

> Run the Solana Developer Platform on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose.

Self-hosting runs the full Solana Developer Platform (API, dashboard, docs, database, and cache) on infrastructure you control, from prebuilt container images. You bring your own authentication (Clerk), Solana RPC, and signing provider.

## What you run

The release's `compose.yml` starts six services:

| Service | Image | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `sdp-api` | `sdp-api` | The API, on port `8787` by default. |
| `sdp-web` | `sdp-web` | The dashboard, on port `3000` by default. |
| `sdp-docs` | `sdp-docs` | These docs, on port `3001` by default. |
| `sdp-migrate` | `sdp-api` | Applies pending database migrations, then exits. |
| `postgres` | `postgres:16-alpine` | The bundled database. You can use an external one instead. |
| `redis` | `redis:7-alpine` | The bundled cache. You can use an external one instead. |

## Start here

- [Quickstart](/docs/self-hosting/quickstart): install the stack and bring it up.
- [First devnet deployment](/docs/self-hosting/first-devnet-deployment): sign in to the dashboard, create a local wallet, and call the API with a wallet-scoped key.
- [Configurator](/docs/self-hosting/configurator): generate a complete `.env` in your browser or terminal.
- [Environment reference](/docs/self-hosting/env-reference): what the variables do and which ones are required.

## Operate

- [Upgrade and backup](/docs/self-hosting/upgrade-and-backup): move to a new release and protect your data.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/self-hosting/troubleshooting): common startup and configuration failures.
- [External co-signers](/docs/self-hosting/external-co-signers): host provider-specific signing services beside the stack.

## Requirements

- A 64-bit Linux or macOS host (x86-64 or Arm64) with Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2.
- Outbound network access to pull images and reach your Solana RPC and Clerk.
- A [Clerk](https://clerk.com) application and a Solana RPC endpoint. The [environment reference](/docs/self-hosting/env-reference) lists the rest.

### Health check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-check

> Returns service health and build metadata.

`GET /health`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is healthy

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · always `ok`

    Health status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Health check timestamp.

  - **`version`** · `string` · required · example `0.1.0`

    Service version.

  - **`environment`** · `string` · required · example `production`

    Runtime environment.

  - **`releaseChannel`** · `string` · required · one of `experimental`, `beta`, `stable` · example `experimental`

    Release channel: which modules this deployment runs.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/health")
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"
{
  "status": "ok",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "environment": "production",
  "releaseChannel": "experimental"
}
```

### Readiness check
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/health/health-readiness

> Performs readiness checks for downstream dependencies.

`GET /health/ready`

Public: this route takes no API key.

## Responses

- **`200`** Service is ready

  - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `ready`, `not_ready` · example `ready`

    Readiness status.

  - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

    Readiness check timestamp.

  - **`revision`** · `string` · required · example `sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc`

    Cloud Run revision serving the request, or `local` outside Cloud Run.

  - **`commit`** · `string` · required · example `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`

    Git commit the serving image was built from, or `local` when the image carries none.

  - **`releaseChannel`** · `string` · required · one of `experimental`, `beta`, `stable` · example `stable`

    Release channel: which modules this deployment runs.

  - **`checks`** · `object` · required

    Dependency health checks.

    - **`database`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Database connectivity status.

    - **`redis`** · `string` · required · one of `ok`, `error` · example `ok`

      Redis connectivity status.

    - **`egress`** · `string` · one of `pending`, `ok`, `unverified` · example `ok`

      Outbound internet connectivity of this instance. `pending` (not ready) while a fresh instance waits for working egress, `ok` once an outbound call succeeded, `unverified` when it stopped waiting and serves anyway. Absent where the deployment does not wait for egress.

- **`503`** Service is not ready

  Same fields as `200`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
curl 'https://api.solana.com/health/ready'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/health/ready", {
  method: "GET"
});
```

```python tab="Python"
import requests

r = requests.get("https://api.solana.com/health/ready")
```

## Example responses

```json tab="200"

  "status": "ready",

  "revision": "sdp-prod-api-public-00042-abc",
```

### Wallets
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/wallets

> Wallet signing provider configuration and wallet management.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/v1/wallets` | [Create wallet](/docs/reference/api/wallets/create-wallet.md) |
