### Submit a withdrawal
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal

> Submits a withdrawal transaction signed by the customer's wallet.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawals`

It works like a deposit submit: SDP checks every signature against the exact built message, records the movement before broadcast, requires an Idempotency-Key, and accepts each built transaction once, with the same `409 CONFLICT` answers. Submit the original signed bytes even after the blockhash expires, since the wallet may already have broadcast them. After an uncertain response, retry with the same key and body, then read the movement instead of building a new withdrawal. Withdrawals stay available while Earn is disabled.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · required · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Idempotency key for safely retrying mutating requests. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; echoed back on the response.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Submit the signed bytes back. Requires the Idempotency-Key header; a retry with the same key resolves the original movement or withdrawal request instead of acting twice.

- **`transactionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_external_wallet_transaction_e7a88258-1d19-48f3-8d0e-81fefa4bf3b3`

  The built transaction being submitted; single-use.

- **`signedTransaction`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 1700 · pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$` · example `AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOAAQABAvSV602SJ67iQCUGLwHzVtPnlMbZqL79wnV/nb+Mi9SJBUpTWpkpIQZNJOhxYNo4fHw1td28kruB5B+oQEEFRI0AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEBAAtzZHAtZXhhbXBsZQA=`

  Base64 wire bytes of the signed transaction. They must be byte-for-byte the built message with only signatures added.

## Responses

- **`200`** The recorded withdrawal

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    - **`withdrawal`** · `object` · required

      One recorded external-wallet vault movement.

      - **`settlementOutcome`** · `string` · one of `delivered`, `cancelled`

      - **`movementId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_movement_a6aed3f5-4f89-4dc6-9d4b-0864021bd80d`

      - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

      - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `kamino`

      - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required · example `7uib8xGAwkaPz4ZGCA6t8sSEid5Yp9ty13PHUweTypx`

      - **`direction`** · `string` · required · one of `deposit`, `withdrawal`

      - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `requested`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `finalized`, `failed`

        The movement's status. `requested` means SDP recorded the signed transaction but has not yet seen it on the network. `confirmed` is optimistic and can still be rolled back; only `finalized` and `failed` are final.

      - **`settlement`** · `string` · required · one of `atomic`, `provider_order`

        How the movement settles. `atomic` completes in one transaction, so you may show it as done at `confirmed` while SDP tracks finality. `provider_order` pays out later through the provider, so chain confirmation alone is not payout: the movement stays `confirmed` until the provider completes it, and only `finalized` means it is done.

      - **`signature`** · `string` · required

        The transaction signature, for explorers.

      - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

        The customer's wallet address.

      - **`amount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

        Requested quantity, denominated in `denomination`.

      - **`denomination`** · `string` · required · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

        Token mint for a deposit; share mint for a withdrawal.

      - **`tokenMint`** · `string` · required · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

        The position's deposit-token mint. Show `tokenAmount` in these units; `amount` and `denomination` carry the onchain quantity, which is shares on a withdrawal.

      - **`tokenAmount`** · `string | null` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

        Quantity in `tokenMint` units. Kamino deposits and all withdrawals require a finalized observation; null beforehand or when the actual debit/payout cannot be observed. Other deposits report their fixed input amount.

      - **`failureReason`** · `string | null` · required

      - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`confirmedAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`settledAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

        ISO 8601 timestamp.

      - **`replayed`** · `boolean`

        True when the idempotency key already produced this movement and nothing was re-sent.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `earn.execute` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(uuidgen)
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawals' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "transactionId": "earn_external_wallet_transaction_0ebe7320-4b8e-4d1a-a5f0-6c2d9e8b1f47",
    "signedTransaction": "AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOA"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"

    "signedTransaction": "AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOA"
```

### List withdrawal options
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-options

> Lists the withdrawal routes a position supports right now: instant, provider order, solver queue and operator redemption, each read from live provider state.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-options`

A position offers instant or provider order, never both; the withdrawal endpoints build whichever it offers. Call this when the customer starts a withdrawal, and let them choose when more than one route is available. Never infer a route from the strategy's `liquidityTerm`.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.read` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

List the withdrawal routes a position supports right now.

- **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

  The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

## Responses

- **`200`** Withdrawal options and their live terms

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

      The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

    - **`instant`** · `boolean` · required

      Whether the withdrawal endpoints build an instant withdrawal for this position. Never true together with `providerOrder`.

    - **`providerRedemptionModes`** · `string[]` · each one of `standard`, `instant`

    - **`providerOrder`** · `boolean` · required

      Whether the withdrawal endpoints build a provider order that pays out later. Never true together with `instant`.

    - **`queued`** · `boolean` · required

      Whether a solver queue accepts requests now. Never infer it from `liquidityTerm`.

    - **`withdrawAuthority`** · `string | null` · required

      The withdrawal authority the queue's vault reports, or null without a queue. Informational: no request takes it.

    - **`queueState`** · `string | null` · required

      The provider queue account, or null without a queue.

    - **`queueAsset`** · `object | null` · required

      Live asset-specific queue limits. Null when this asset has no queue configuration.

      - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Base58 Solana mint address.

      - **`allowWithdrawals`** · `boolean` · required

        Whether this asset's queue currently accepts new requests.

      - **`secondsToMaturity`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `86400`

        Seconds after the request is created, by the cluster clock, before a solver may fulfill it.

      - **`minimumSecondsToDeadline`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · example `3600`

        Shortest solver window accepted after maturity.

      - **`maximumSecondsToDeadline`** · `integer` · required · greater than 0 · max 7776000 · example `7776000`

        Longest solver window accepted after maturity.

      - **`minimumDiscountBps`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 10000 · example `0`

      - **`maximumDiscountBps`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 10000 · example `500`

      - **`minimumShares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `1`

        Smallest request accepted by the queue, in share units.

      - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38 · example `6`

    - **`parRedemption`** · `object | null` · required

      Live operator redemption terms. Null when this strategy offers no operator redemption.

      - **`intermediateMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Token created or delegated by the request transaction and later burned by the operator.

      - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Token the operator pays when the redemption completes.

      - **`minimumShares`** · `string | null` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `1`

        Smallest operator redemption request funded by shares, in position-share units. Null while the provider's rate is unavailable, which also blocks share-funded requests.

      - **`minimumIntermediateAmount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `0.000001`

        Smallest request over intermediate the owner already holds, in intermediate-token units.

      - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38 · example `6`

      - **`assetDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38 · example `6`

      - **`cancelable`** · `boolean` · required

        Whether the owner may revoke an open request before the operator completes it.

      - **`operatorSettled`** · `boolean` · required · always `true`

        Always true: a provider operator must complete the eventual asset payout.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `earn.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`501`** The provider does not support this operation.

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

### Preview a withdrawal request
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-queued-withdrawal-preview

> Previews a withdrawal request: a solver queue's discounted payout and timing, or an operator redemption's intermediate-token conversion and payout.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/queued-withdrawal-previews`

Check the mechanism against the position's withdrawal options first, and resolve every `blockingIssues` entry before the customer confirms. The preview is read-only and safe to retry. It does not check the wallet's balance, so keep `shares` within the position's `withdrawableShares`.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.read` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Preview a solver-queue or operator-redemption request against live provider limits. Read-only: nothing is built or persisted.

Any of:

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

    Shares to place in the withdrawal request, in share units.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · always `solverQueue`

    Selects the solver queue, which is also the default when omitted. Operator redemptions must set `mechanism` explicitly.

  - **`discountBps`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 10000 · example `25`

    Discount offered to a solver, in basis points. It must stay inside the live queueAsset minimum and maximum.

  - **`deadlineSeconds`** · `integer` · required · greater than 0 · max 7776000 · example `86400`

    Solver window after maturity, in seconds. It must stay inside the live queueAsset minimum and maximum.

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

    Shares to place in the withdrawal request, in share units.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

    Selects an operator redemption, which takes no solver discount or deadline.

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`intermediateAmount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `2000`

    Intermediate token the owner already holds outside any request (such as a cancelled request's wYLDS) to redeem at par, in that token's units. Send instead of `shares`, never with it.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

    Selects an operator redemption, which takes no solver discount or deadline.

## Responses

- **`200`** Expected request terms

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    Any of:

    - **object**

      - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

        The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

      - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Base58 Solana mint address.

      - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

        Positive decimal string with at least one non-zero digit; never a float.

      - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

      - **`assets`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `9.975`

        Expected payout after the discount, in `assetMint` units.

      - **`assetDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

      - **`discountBps`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 10000

      - **`maturityTimestamp`** · `string` · required · pattern `^\d+$` · example `1789722000`

        Unix time, in seconds, when a solver may start fulfilling the request.

      - **`deadlineTimestamp`** · `string` · required · pattern `^\d+$` · example `1789808400`

        Unix time, in seconds, of the request's deadline. A solver may fulfill it until this time; cancellation is allowed only after it.

      - **`blockingIssues`** · `object[]` · required

        - **`code`** · `string` · required · example `SHARE_LOCKED`

        - **`message`** · `string` · required

    - **object**

      - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

        The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

      - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

      - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

        Position shares the request burns, in share units; "0" when it redeems intermediate the owner already holds.

      - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

      - **`intermediateMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Token the request creates or delegates for later operator settlement.

      - **`intermediateAmount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

        Expected intermediate-token amount, in that token's units.

      - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

        Base58 Solana mint address.

      - **`assets`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

        Expected par payout when the operator completes the redemption.

      - **`assetDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

      - **`blockingIssues`** · `object[]` · required

        - **`code`** · `string` · required · example `SHARE_LOCKED`

        - **`message`** · `string` · required

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

      Request identifier for tracing.

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  Same fields as `400`.

### Build a withdrawal request transaction
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-transaction

> Builds an unsigned withdrawal request transaction for a position, for the customer's wallet to sign.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-transactions`

A solver queue request escrows shares; an operator redemption converts shares into an intermediate token that the operator settles later. Neither transaction pays the customer. Save the `withdrawalRequestId` the submit returns and track the request until it is fulfilled, canceled, or failed.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Build a keyed asynchronous withdrawal request. A solver request escrows shares; an operator redemption converts them into the provider's intermediate token, or delegates intermediate the owner already holds. Neither action pays assets.

Any of:

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

    Shares to place in the withdrawal request, in share units.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · always `solverQueue`

    Selects the solver queue, which is also the default when omitted. Operator redemptions must set `mechanism` explicitly.

  - **`discountBps`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 10000 · example `25`

    Discount offered to a solver, in basis points. It must stay inside the live queueAsset minimum and maximum.

  - **`deadlineSeconds`** · `integer` · required · greater than 0 · max 7776000 · example `86400`

    Solver window after maturity, in seconds. It must stay inside the live queueAsset minimum and maximum.

  - **`feePayer`** · `string` · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

    Pay for this transaction from a wallet your backend controls instead of the customer's. The named address becomes the fee payer: it pays the network fee, funds any share-account rent, and must sign alongside the customer. Co-sign on your backend before you submit. The build returns 400, naming the fee payer, when it cannot pay. Sending the customer's own address keeps the default: the customer pays and signs alone.

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

    Shares to place in the withdrawal request, in share units.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

    Selects an operator redemption, which takes no solver discount or deadline.

  - **`feePayer`** · `string` · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

    Pay for this transaction from a wallet your backend controls instead of the customer's. The named address becomes the fee payer: it pays the network fee, funds any share-account rent, and must sign alongside the customer. Co-sign on your backend before you submit. The build returns 400, naming the fee payer, when it cannot pay. Sending the customer's own address keeps the default: the customer pays and signs alone.

- **object**

  - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

    The position's ID, from the positions list or the deposit submit response.

  - **`intermediateAmount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `2000`

    Intermediate token the owner already holds outside any request (such as a cancelled request's wYLDS) to redeem at par, in that token's units. Send instead of `shares`, never with it.

  - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

    Selects an operator redemption, which takes no solver discount or deadline.

  - **`feePayer`** · `string` · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

    Pay for this transaction from a wallet your backend controls instead of the customer's. The named address becomes the fee payer: it pays the network fee, funds any share-account rent, and must sign alongside the customer. Co-sign on your backend before you submit. The build returns 400, naming the fee payer, when it cannot pay. Sending the customer's own address keeps the default: the customer pays and signs alone.

## Responses

- **`200`** Unsigned withdrawal request transaction

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    - **`transaction`** · `object` · required

      Any of:

      - **mechanism: "solverQueue"**

        - **`transactionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_external_wallet_transaction_e7a88258-1d19-48f3-8d0e-81fefa4bf3b3`

        - **`transaction`** · `string` · required

          Base64 wire bytes of the unsigned transaction. Add every required signature without changing the message, then submit through SDP. The blockhash bounds when the network can first accept it; retain the original signed bytes for recovery.

        - **`lastValidBlockHeight`** · `string` · required · example `361186610`

          Last block height at which the network can first accept this transaction. This is a block height, not a slot or timestamp.

        - **`sponsored`** · `boolean` · required · example `false`

          Always false: SDP does not pay an external wallet's fees. The customer's wallet pays, or the `feePayer` you name.

        - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

          The customer's wallet address.

        - **`feePayer`** · `string` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

          The `feePayer` your build request named. When present, the transaction needs the fee payer's signature as well as the customer's: co-sign on your backend before you submit, or the submit refuses it. When omitted, the customer signs alone and pays the fee.

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `kamino`

        - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required · example `7uib8xGAwkaPz4ZGCA6t8sSEid5Yp9ty13PHUweTypx`

          The strategy's onchain address at the provider. It identifies the instrument; never send funds to it.

        - **`tokenMint`** · `string` · required · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

        - **`shareMint`** · `string` · required · example `hXm2xSRF5PLKGMrTvAWqKhR76MuJX5dAabeSChkjqu2`

        - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

        - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `solverQueue`

### Submit a withdrawal request
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request

> Submits a withdrawal request transaction signed by the customer's wallet.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests`

SDP checks every signature against the exact built message, records the request before broadcast, then sends it. Idempotency-Key is required: a retry with the same key returns the original request, and each built transaction can be submitted once. Reusing a key with a different body, or submitting one build under a second key, returns `409 CONFLICT`. An expired build can still be submitted late. If its reservation was released or replaced, SDP accepts it only once the exact signed transaction is finalized as successful, so after a `409 CONFLICT` retry the same bytes and key until that shows. A late operator redemption whose original cycle already closed is refused for operator reconciliation, so it cannot claim a newer request at the same address. A transaction that recovery finds finalized as failed returns `400 TRANSACTION_FAILED`; build a new one. A recovery RPC outage returns `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`: retry the original bytes and key. An unresolved 16-signature history window returns `503` and needs support to reconcile. An expired operator redemption build whose creation history is unavailable also returns `503`: keep and retry the original signed intent rather than signing a replacement.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.execute` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · required · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Idempotency key for safely retrying mutating requests. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; echoed back on the response.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Submit the signed bytes back. Requires the Idempotency-Key header; a retry with the same key resolves the original movement or withdrawal request instead of acting twice.

- **`transactionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_external_wallet_transaction_e7a88258-1d19-48f3-8d0e-81fefa4bf3b3`

  The built transaction being submitted; single-use.

- **`signedTransaction`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 1700 · pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$` · example `AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOAAQABAvSV602SJ67iQCUGLwHzVtPnlMbZqL79wnV/nb+Mi9SJBUpTWpkpIQZNJOhxYNo4fHw1td28kruB5B+oQEEFRI0AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEBAAtzZHAtZXhhbXBsZQA=`

  Base64 wire bytes of the signed transaction. They must be byte-for-byte the built message with only signatures added.

## Responses

- **`200`** The recorded withdrawal request

    - **`withdrawalRequest`** · `object` · required

      Any of:

      - **mechanism: "solverQueue"**

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `veda`

        - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required

          The strategy's onchain address.

        - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

          The customer's wallet address.

        - **`requestAddress`** · `string` · required

          Provider request account address.

        - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `creating`, `pending`, `fulfillable`, `expiredCancelable`, `cancelling`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, `closedOrUnknown`, `failed`

          The request's status. Only `fulfilled`, `cancelled` and `failed` are final. Keep tracking every other status, `closedOrUnknown` included: SDP resolves it from a finalized close event.

        - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

          Base58 Solana mint address.

          Positive decimal string with at least one non-zero digit; never a float.

        - **`quotedAssets`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          Expected payout at request creation, in `assetMint` units. Not a settled amount.

## Example request

```bash tab="cURL"
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(uuidgen)
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "transactionId": "earn_external_wallet_withdrawal_request_transaction_54c50679-1b52-494d-84fa-106df66452ff",
    "signedTransaction": "AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOA"
  }'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
// Reuse this key when you retry this request.
const idempotencyKey = crypto.randomUUID();
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": idempotencyKey,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "transactionId": "earn_external_wallet_withdrawal_request_transaction_54c50679-1b52-494d-84fa-106df66452ff",
    "signedTransaction": "AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOA"
  })
});
```

```python tab="Python"

  json={
    "transactionId": "earn_external_wallet_withdrawal_request_transaction_54c50679-1b52-494d-84fa-106df66452ff",

  })
```

### List withdrawal requests
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/list-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-requests

> Lists one customer wallet's withdrawal requests, one page at a time.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests`

`ownerAddress` is required. On startup and after reconnecting, pass `settled=false` to restore every request that still needs fulfillment, classification or cancellation, and page until `hasMore` is false.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.read` action.

## Query parameters

- **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

  The customer's wallet address: an external wallet, so SDP holds no key for it. It signs, owns the shares, and pays the network fee unless the build names a `feePayer`. It must decode to a 32-byte public key; a base58 string that matches the pattern but does not decode returns 400.

- **`limit`** · `integer` · min 1 · max 100 · default `20`

  Page size, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

- **`before`** · `string` · min length 1

  The previous page's `nextCursor`. Omit it for the first page.

- **`status`** · `string` · one of `creating`, `pending`, `fulfillable`, `expiredCancelable`, `cancelling`, `closedOrUnknown`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, `failed`

- **`settled`** · `string` · one of `true`, `false`

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `veda`

        - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required

          The strategy's onchain address.

        - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

          The customer's wallet address.

        - **`requestAddress`** · `string` · required

          Provider request account address.

        - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `creating`, `pending`, `fulfillable`, `expiredCancelable`, `cancelling`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, `closedOrUnknown`, `failed`

          The request's status. Only `fulfilled`, `cancelled` and `failed` are final. Keep tracking every other status, `closedOrUnknown` included: SDP resolves it from a finalized close event.

        - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

        - **`shareMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

        - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `10`

          Position shares the request burns, in share units; "0" when it redeems intermediate the owner already holds.

        - **`quotedAssets`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          Expected payout at request creation, in `assetMint` units. Not a settled amount.

        - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

        - **`assetDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

        - **`nonce`** · `string | null` · required

        - **`creationTimestamp`** · `string | null` · required · pattern `^\d+$`

        - **`creationSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          The request-creation transaction. Its confirmation does not prove a payout.

        - **`cancelSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          The cancellation transaction, once one is submitted.

        - **`closingSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          Provider-authenticated fulfillment or cancellation transaction, when known.

        - **`assetsPaid`** · `string | null` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          The payout SDP observed at fulfillment, in `assetMint` units; null until then.

        - **`failureReason`** · `string | null` · required

        - **`fulfilledAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`cancelledAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`createdAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`updatedAt`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`replayed`** · `boolean`

        - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · always `operatorRedemption`

        - **`intermediateMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

        - **`intermediateAmount`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          Positive decimal string with at least one non-zero digit; never a float.

        - **`discountBps`** · `any` · required

        - **`maturityTimestamp`** · `any` · required

        - **`deadlineTimestamp`** · `any` · required

    - **`hasMore`** · `boolean` · required

    - **`nextCursor`** · `string | null` · required

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `earn.read` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

  Same fields as `400`.

### Get a withdrawal request
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/get-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request

> Gets one withdrawal request with its latest recorded status.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-requests/{withdrawalRequestId}`

Creating a request escrows shares or converts them to an intermediate token; it does not pay out. Only `fulfilled`, `cancelled` and `failed` are final. Keep polling a `closedOrUnknown` request: SDP has not yet confirmed whether it paid out or returned the customer's tokens.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.read` action.

## Path parameters

- **`withdrawalRequestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_vault_withdrawal_request_3c905ad2-c92c-4258-9675-1899c41569b9`

  The `withdrawalRequestId` a request submit returned.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

### Build a cancellation transaction
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancel-transaction

> Builds an unsigned transaction that cancels a withdrawal request, for the customer's wallet to sign.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancel-transactions`

A solver queue request can be canceled only at `expiredCancelable`, because a solver may fulfill it until its deadline; before then the build returns `409 CONFLICT`. An operator redemption that allows cancellation can be canceled while `pending`, which leaves the customer holding the intermediate token, not the original shares. Requires `earn.manage`. Cancellation stays available without production access and while Earn is disabled; a suspended organization still cannot authenticate.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.manage` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Build a cancellation for the customer's wallet to sign. A solver queue request becomes cancelable at `expiredCancelable`; an operator redemption that allows cancellation can be canceled while `pending`.

- **`withdrawalRequestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_vault_withdrawal_request_3c905ad2-c92c-4258-9675-1899c41569b9`

- **`feePayer`** · `string` · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

  Pay for this transaction from a wallet your backend controls instead of the customer's. The named address becomes the fee payer: it pays the network fee, funds any share-account rent, and must sign alongside the customer. Co-sign on your backend before you submit. The build returns 400, naming the fee payer, when it cannot pay. Sending the customer's own address keeps the default: the customer pays and signs alone.

## Responses

- **`200`** Unsigned cancellation transaction

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    - **`transaction`** · `object` · required

      A cancellation for the customer's wallet to sign.

      - **`transactionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_external_wallet_transaction_e7a88258-1d19-48f3-8d0e-81fefa4bf3b3`

      - **`transaction`** · `string` · required

        Base64 wire bytes of the unsigned transaction. Add every required signature without changing the message, then submit through SDP. The blockhash bounds when the network can first accept it; retain the original signed bytes for recovery.

      - **`lastValidBlockHeight`** · `string` · required · example `361186610`

        Last block height at which the network can first accept this transaction. This is a block height, not a slot or timestamp.

      - **`sponsored`** · `boolean` · required · example `false`

        Always false: SDP does not pay an external wallet's fees. The customer's wallet pays, or the `feePayer` you name.

      - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

        The customer's wallet address.

      - **`feePayer`** · `string` · example `3nMFwZXwY1s1M5s8vYAHqd4wGs4iSxXE4LRoUMMYqEgF`

        The `feePayer` your build request named. When present, the transaction needs the fee payer's signature as well as the customer's: co-sign on your backend before you submit, or the submit refuses it. When omitted, the customer signs alone and pays the fee.

      - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `kamino`

      - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required · example `7uib8xGAwkaPz4ZGCA6t8sSEid5Yp9ty13PHUweTypx`

        The strategy's onchain address at the provider. It identifies the instrument; never send funds to it.

      - **`tokenMint`** · `string` · required · example `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU`

      - **`shareMint`** · `string` · required · example `hXm2xSRF5PLKGMrTvAWqKhR76MuJX5dAabeSChkjqu2`

      - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

      - **`withdrawalRequestId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_vault_withdrawal_request_3c905ad2-c92c-4258-9675-1899c41569b9`

      - **`action`** · `string` · required · always `cancel`

      - **`mechanism`** · `string` · required · one of `solverQueue`, `operatorRedemption`

      - **`requestAddress`** · `string` · required

        Provider request account address.

  - **`meta`** · `object` · required

    Response metadata.

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

    - **`timestamp`** · `string` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

      ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **`400`** Bad Request

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

      Machine-readable error code.

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

    - **`requestId`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `req_example`

      Request identifier for tracing.

- **`401`** Unauthorized

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`403`** Forbidden. Requires the `earn.manage` action: an API key must hold it (a module's `manage` or `execute` also covers its `read`), and a signed-in member's organization role must include it. Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`404`** Not Found

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`409`** Conflict

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`429`** Too Many Requests

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`500`** Internal Server Error

  Same fields as `400`.

- **`501`** The provider does not support this operation.

  - **`error`** · `object` · required

    Standard error payload.

    - **`code`** · `string` · required

    - **`message`** · `string` · required

      Human-readable error message.

    - **`details`** · `object`

      Optional error details for debugging.

      - **`*`** · `any`

  - **`meta`** · `object`

- **`503`** Service Unavailable

### Submit a cancellation
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/earn/create-earn-external-wallet-withdrawal-request-cancellation

> Submits a cancellation transaction signed by the customer's wallet.

> **Earn is under active development.** Features, API endpoints, and docs may change.

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-request-cancellations`

SDP verifies it, records it before broadcast, and returns the withdrawal request. Idempotency-Key is required, with the same `409 CONFLICT` answers as the other submits. Requires `earn.manage`, and stays available without production access and while Earn is disabled; a suspended organization still cannot authenticate. Keep polling until the request is `cancelled`, `fulfilled` or `failed`, because a fulfillment can race the cancellation.

Requires an [API key](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) with the `earn.manage` action.

## Headers

- **`x-project-id`** · `string` · min length 1 · example `prj_example`

  Required for dashboard sessions. API keys use their assigned project.

- **`Idempotency-Key`** · `string` · required · pattern `^[\x20-\x7e]{1,255}$` · example `idempotency_example_12345`

  Idempotency key for safely retrying mutating requests. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; echoed back on the response.

## Request body

`application/json` · required

Submit the signed bytes back. Requires the Idempotency-Key header; a retry with the same key resolves the original movement or withdrawal request instead of acting twice.

- **`transactionId`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 128 · example `earn_external_wallet_transaction_e7a88258-1d19-48f3-8d0e-81fefa4bf3b3`

  The built transaction being submitted; single-use.

- **`signedTransaction`** · `string` · required · min length 1 · max length 1700 · pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$` · example `AUyx/sEc49/1l6jxo3nbViPAIUqdrXCo8Qx5SfDvIbtUI0zex3Bi6Cyhhn1QTVU8zWDzXTRyIX2aCmq9v7yk5AOAAQABAvSV602SJ67iQCUGLwHzVtPnlMbZqL79wnV/nb+Mi9SJBUpTWpkpIQZNJOhxYNo4fHw1td28kruB5B+oQEEFRI0AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEBAAtzZHAtZXhhbXBsZQA=`

  Base64 wire bytes of the signed transaction. They must be byte-for-byte the built message with only signatures added.

## Responses

- **`200`** The withdrawal request with its cancellation recorded

  - **`data`** · `object` · required

    - **`withdrawalRequest`** · `object` · required

      Any of:

      - **mechanism: "solverQueue"**

        - **`withdrawalRequestId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_vault_withdrawal_request_3c905ad2-c92c-4258-9675-1899c41569b9`

        - **`positionId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_position_2f8b6b04-7147-487e-b760-b1caa4fbcb8b`

        - **`provider`** · `string` · required · example `veda`

        - **`providerReference`** · `string` · required

          The strategy's onchain address.

        - **`ownerAddress`** · `string` · required · example `9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM`

          The customer's wallet address.

        - **`requestAddress`** · `string` · required

          Provider request account address.

        - **`status`** · `string` · required · one of `creating`, `pending`, `fulfillable`, `expiredCancelable`, `cancelling`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, `closedOrUnknown`, `failed`

          The request's status. Only `fulfilled`, `cancelled` and `failed` are final. Keep tracking every other status, `closedOrUnknown` included: SDP resolves it from a finalized close event.

        - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

        - **`shareMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

          Base58 Solana mint address.

        - **`shares`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          Positive decimal string with at least one non-zero digit; never a float.

        - **`quotedAssets`** · `string` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          Expected payout at request creation, in `assetMint` units. Not a settled amount.

        - **`shareDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

        - **`assetDecimals`** · `integer` · required · min 0 · max 38

        - **`nonce`** · `string | null` · required

        - **`creationTimestamp`** · `string | null` · required · pattern `^\d+$`

        - **`creationSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          The request-creation transaction. Its confirmation does not prove a payout.

        - **`cancelSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          The cancellation transaction, once one is submitted.

        - **`closingSignature`** · `string | null` · required

          Provider-authenticated fulfillment or cancellation transaction, when known.

        - **`assetsPaid`** · `string | null` · required · max length 128 · pattern `^(?=.*[1-9])\d+(\.\d+)?$` · example `25`

          The payout SDP observed at fulfillment, in `assetMint` units; null until then.

        - **`failureReason`** · `string | null` · required

        - **`fulfilledAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`cancelledAt`** · `string | null` · required · format `date-time` · example `2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`

          ISO 8601 timestamp.

        - **`maturityTimestamp`** · `string` · required · pattern `^\d+$`

        - **`deadlineTimestamp`** · `string` · required · pattern `^\d+$`

      - **mechanism: "operatorRedemption"**

        - **`withdrawalRequestId`** · `string` · required · example `earn_vault_withdrawal_request_3c905ad2-c92c-4258-9675-1899c41569b9`

        - **`assetMint`** · `string` · required · min length 32 · max length 44 · pattern `^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$` · example `2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo`

## Docs

### AI resources
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/docs-for-ai

> Machine-readable SDP docs, the agent skill, and setup for coding agents.

Give your coding agent these entry points. They cover the supported public surface only.

## Machine-readable resources

- [llms.txt](/docs/ai/llms.txt): canonical URLs, supported surfaces, the public endpoint families, and the key pages to start from. The site root serves it too, at `/llms.txt`.
- [llms-full.txt](/docs/ai/llms-full.txt): the full text of every published page, the API reference included, in one file. Also at `/llms-full.txt`.
- Markdown pages: add `.md` to any docs URL (`/docs/reference/docs-for-ai.md`), or request the page with `Accept: text/markdown`. `/docs.md` lists every page. Each page's **Copy page** menu copies the same Markdown.
- [SKILL.md](/SKILL.md): an agent skill with SDP's rules for environments, API key grants, idempotency, and prepare versus execute. The sidebar's **Agent setup** menu has the install command for your agent. The agent-neutral one is `npx skills add solana-foundation/solana-developer-platform --skill sdp-docs`.
- [API reference](/docs/reference/api): every public operation, generated from the public OpenAPI contract.
- [OpenAPI JSON](https://api.solana.com/openapi.json): the public API contract itself.
- [API llms.txt](https://api.solana.com/llms.txt): the API's own discovery file, with its endpoint families and how to authenticate.
- [Postman collection](/docs/reference/postman-collection): the public API as a collection, generated from the same contract.

## Recommended ingestion order

1. Start with [llms.txt](/docs/ai/llms.txt).
2. Load [llms-full.txt](/docs/ai/llms-full.txt) when you need every page.
3. Use the [API reference](/docs/reference/api) and [OpenAPI JSON](https://api.solana.com/openapi.json) for exact request and response schemas.
4. Use the product guides for workflow order, operational limits, and supported patterns.

## Scope

Treat the public docs as the source of truth over internal implementation details. Hidden and internal-only route families are left out of every resource on this page.

## Getting Started

### Set up your workspace
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/setup-organization

> Create your account and organization, which comes with a Sandbox and a Production project.

Everything you do in SDP belongs to an **organization**, your team's workspace. An organization holds **projects**, and each project has its own API keys, wallets, and members. This guide creates your account and organization.

### 1. Create your account

Go to [platform.solana.com](https://platform.solana.com) and click **Create account**. The sign-in screen has the same button at the top right. When sign-up is closed, these buttons read **Join the waitlist** and **Request access** instead.

Enter your email address and a password to create your account.

### 2. Create your organization

After you sign in, **Name your organization** asks for an **Organization name**. Enter it and click **Create organization**. You become the organization's admin. If you've been invited to an organization, accept the invitation or pick the organization from the list instead.

To switch organizations or projects later, click your organization's name at the top of the sidebar.

<img src="/docs/images/getting-started/org-switcher.png" alt="Organization switcher with your organizations, the project list and the organization ID" width="262" height="322" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto" }} />

### 3. Work in a project

Your organization comes with two projects: **Default Sandbox Project** on devnet and **Default Production Project** on mainnet. Build in the sandbox project. Production can't move money until SDP approves your organization; see [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet). To read projects with an API key, see the [Projects API reference](/docs/reference/api/projects).

### 4. Next steps

- [Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets) for signing transactions
- [Create API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) for programmatic access
- [Send your first payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment)
- [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet) when your sandbox integration is ready

### Create a wallet
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/setup-wallets

> Set up a custody provider and create wallets for signing transactions.

A **custody wallet** is a Solana keypair whose key a custody provider holds. SDP sends each signing request to the provider that holds the wallet's key. Set up a provider, then create wallets for transfers and other onchain operations.

## Supported providers

| Provider | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Privy** | Embedded wallet infrastructure platform |
| **[Fireblocks](/docs/wallet-operations/fireblocks)** | Digital asset infrastructure company |
| **Coinbase CDP** | Embedded wallets for developers |
| **Para** | Wallet and authentication suite |
| **Turnkey** | Non-custodial wallet infrastructure platform |
| **DFNS** | Digital asset wallet infrastructure |
| **IBM Digital Asset Haven** | Institutional custody on IBM Digital Asset Haven |
| **Anchorage** | Regulated institutional crypto custody |
| **Utila** | Vault-backed wallet signing through service accounts |

- [Connect Fireblocks](/docs/wallet-operations/fireblocks): Connect your own Fireblocks workspace for production custody.

**Dashboard**

### 1. Open wallet setup

Open **Wallets** in the sidebar and click **Create wallet**. Once the project has wallets, the button reads **Create a wallet**. Only organization admins can create wallets. Complete [organization setup](/docs/guides/setup-organization) first if needed.

### 2. Choose a custody provider

Under **Which provider holds the keys?**, select a provider. You can't change it after the wallet exists. When your project can use only one provider, it's already selected and the question isn't shown.

### 3. Choose whose account holds the keys

If you can connect your own account for the provider, the page asks whose account holds the keys, such as **Whose Privy account holds the keys?** When there's a choice, nothing is preselected.

- **SDP's Privy account**: for trying SDP out in Sandbox. It has no wallet policy and nothing to set up.
- **Your own Privy account**: connect it with its app ID and secret. Production accepts only your own account; see [Go to mainnet](/docs/guides/go-to-mainnet).

### 4. Create the first wallet

With SDP's account, enter a **Wallet label** and click **Create wallet**. The wallet's page opens with its address and balance.

With your own account, keep or rename the **Credential label**, and enter your **Privy app ID** and **Privy app secret**. Under **Wallet details**, enter a **Wallet label**. Click **Connect and create wallet**: SDP checks the credentials with Privy, then creates the wallet, which appears on **Wallets**.

![Privy provider setup with example credentials and a masked secret](/images/go-to-mainnet/04-connect-privy.png)

The first wallet in a provider account is a transfer wallet.

### 5. Create more wallets

On **Wallets**, click **Create a wallet** and select the provider if asked. The account question lists SDP's account where it's offered, each of your connections, and **Connect another Privy account**. A connection that isn't ready shows what it needs, with a link to fix it.

For SDP's account or an existing connection, enter a **Wallet label**, pick a **Purpose** (it starts on **Transfers**), and click **Create wallet**. **Connect another Privy account** works as in step 4.

A connection signs only with its current credentials. If you rotate or remove them while a request is signing, that request returns `409 CONFLICT` with `details.reason` set to `runtime_execution_unavailable`. Retry it as [Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency) describes for that operation. A transfer that recorded the failure replays it under the same `Idempotency-Key`, so send the transfer again with a new key.

**API**

#### 1. Set up the provider in the dashboard

Setting up a custody provider takes `wallets.configure`, and no API key can hold a `configure` action. An organization admin sets it up once per project, signed in to the dashboard (see the **Dashboard** tab), which calls `POST /v1/wallets/initialize` with that session. The same call with an API key returns `403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` with `details.action` set to `wallets.configure`.

Production projects take only your own provider account. `POST /v1/wallets/initialize` sets up SDP's account of the provider (Managed custody), so in a Production project it returns `403` with `details.reason` set to `custody_mode_not_allowed`. Connect your own account to the project in the dashboard instead. Then create wallets in that connection with `connectionId`, using an API key that holds `wallets.manage`:

```bash title="Terminal"
export IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(uuidgen)

curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "connectionId": "cconn_123",
    "label": "Treasury wallet"
  }'
```

#### 2. Create more wallets

Every wallet names the provider account it lives under: `provider` for SDP's account of that provider (Managed), or `connectionId` for a connection your project added. Send exactly one of them; a body with both or neither returns `400`. There is no default account to fall back to.

**curl**

```bash
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(uuidgen)
curl -X POST 'https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $IDEMPOTENCY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "privy",
    "label": "Treasury wallet",
    "purpose": "transfer"
  }'
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// Reuse this key when you retry this request.
const idempotencyKey = crypto.randomUUID();
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Idempotency-Key": idempotencyKey,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    "provider": "privy",
    "label": "Treasury wallet",
    "purpose": "transfer"
  })
});
```

**Java**

```java title="CreateWallet.java"
String idempotencyKey = java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString();
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sf_...")
    .header("Idempotency-Key", idempotencyKey)
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "provider": "privy",
          "label": "Treasury wallet",
          "purpose": "transfer"
        }"""))
    .build();
```

`purpose` is optional and defaults to `transfer`. Only a `transfer` wallet can be the source of a transfer, transfer batch, or recurring payment; any other purpose is refused with `403` and `details.reason` set to `wallet_purpose`. Reuse the same `Idempotency-Key` when you retry a wallet creation.

#### 3. List wallets

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..."
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="list-wallets.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary", {
  headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer sf_..." },
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.wallets includes id, walletId, publicKey, provider, label, purpose, and status
```

**Java**

```java title="ListWallets.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sf_...")
    .GET()
    .build();
```

Every operation that signs names its wallet; there is no default wallet. Transfers take the wallet's `id` (`cwlt_…`) as `sourceCustodyWalletId`, and other modules' pages name their field. An API key limited to selected wallets lists the same `id` in `walletIds`.

```typescript title="transfer-request.ts"
const body = {
  sourceCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_123", // `id` from GET /v1/wallets
  destination: "7xKXz...9fGh",
  token: "9aBCd...4eEf",
  amount: "100.00",
};
```
