### Payouts and disbursements
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/send-payouts

> Pay many recipients in one batch, retry without paying anyone twice, and reconcile a payout run with SDP.

A payout run pays many recipients at once: marketplace sellers, payroll, affiliates, royalties. Use `POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches` when every recipient is a saved counterparty account. To pay arbitrary Solana addresses, call `POST /v1/payments/transfers` once per recipient and reconcile the transfer ids it returns.

## Native transfer batches

One request creates a durable batch, chunks its recipients into Solana transactions, and returns the batch, recipient, and transfer records:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfer-batches \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3f0c9e7a-5b1d-4c2e-9a8f-6d4b2e1c0a97" \
  -d '{
    "externalId": "payroll-2026-05",
    "sourceCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_123",
    "token": "9aBCd...4eEf",
    "recipients": [
      {
        "externalId": "row_4837",
        "counterpartyId": "cpty_4837",
        "counterpartyAccountId": "cpacct_4837",
        "amount": "150.00"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

Each recipient names a counterparty account (`cpacct_…`) that is an active `crypto_wallet` account in the project. `counterpartyId` is optional; if you pass it, it must be that account's counterparty. An unknown, archived or mismatched account returns `404`. An account whose address changes while the batch is being prepared returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_DESTINATION_CHANGED` naming it in `error.details.counterpartyAccountIds`; nothing is sent, so send the request again. A batch takes up to 500 recipients.

The two ids do different jobs:

- **`Idempotency-Key`** (required) identifies this one request. Reuse it to retry that exact request after a timeout; recipient order does not change the request. Any unique value works, such as a UUID.
- **`externalId`** (required: a batch without one returns `400`) identifies the payout run. Derive it from your own data, such as the pay period, so every attempt at the run carries the same value. See [One batch per payout run](#one-batch-per-payout-run).

Use `GET /v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}` to inspect recipient and chunk outcomes.

Batch execution does not add a priority fee. The estimate reports
`priorityFeeLamports: "0"`.

### One batch per payout run

The batch `externalId` names the payout run, and it is unique per project and source wallet. Whatever `Idempotency-Key` it carries, a batch with an `externalId` already used on that wallet never pays anyone again:

- The same request, from the same API key, returns the existing batch as it stands. A worker that restarts with a fresh key gets the original run back.
- Any other request (different recipients or amounts, or another API key) returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_RUN_EXISTS` with the existing batch in `error.details.batchId`. A replay only goes to the API key that sent the run, so after a key rotation the new key gets the 409: read the batch by its id instead of resending.

Derive the `externalId` from data you already have, so a worker that crashes and restarts computes the same value without storing anything: `payroll-2026-05`, `invoice-run-8812`. Never generate it at random: a random value is new on every attempt and protects nothing. New recipients go in a new run with a new `externalId`, never in a renamed copy of a run that was already sent.

```ts title="payroll-worker.ts"
// Safe to run again after a crash: the run's id comes from the period, not from storage.
const externalId = `payroll-${period}`;
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfer-batches", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ externalId, sourceCustodyWalletId, token, recipients }),
});
const body = await response.json();
// 200: this run's batch, new or replayed. 409 TRANSFER_BATCH_RUN_EXISTS: the run was
// already sent with a different body; read error.details.batchId instead of resending.
// A 5xx may come after the run was sent: its outcome is unknown, so run again with the
// same externalId, which returns the batch if it exists. A 4xx (a 409
// AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM, say) is refused before anything is sent: report it.
let batchId: string;
if (response.ok) {
  batchId = body.data.batch.id;
} else if (body.error.code === "TRANSFER_BATCH_RUN_EXISTS") {
  batchId = body.error.details.batchId;
} else if (response.status >= 500) {
  throw new Error(`Payout run ${externalId} has an unknown outcome: run it again`);
} else {
  throw new Error(`Payout run ${externalId} was refused: ${body.error.code}`);
}
```

### Recovering from a partial failure

A batch with `failed` recipients paid some recipients and not others. A `failed` recipient was not paid: its transaction never reached the network, or the network rejected it. Its `error` says why; when the source wallet could not cover the amount, it reads "The wallet used for this payment does not have enough funds", so fund the wallet before you retry. To finish the run, retry the batch:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}/retry \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 8b2e4f1c-7d3a-4e9b-a6c5-1f0d9e8c7b6a"
```

The retry sends only the batch's `failed` recipients, to the addresses the batch recorded for them, from the same wallet, and returns the batch with those recipients `processing` again. Recipients still `pending` or `processing` may still land, so they are never sent again. Each resent recipient keeps its row in the batch and links to its new transfer.

- Use a new `Idempotency-Key` for each retry you mean to send. The same key never sends again, including after a timeout or a server error, so resend a lost answer under the same key. It returns the saved response while that is stored, which can still show recipients `processing`: read the batch with `GET /v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}` for its current state. If recipients fail again later, a retry under that old key sends nothing.
- Any API key that may send from the batch's wallet can retry it, not only the one that created it.
- A batch with nothing `failed` returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_NOTHING_TO_RETRY`, and a retry that loses to a concurrent one returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_RETRY_CLAIMED`. Nothing is sent. While a batch is `processing`, a recipient its request never sent becomes `failed` only once that request can no longer send it, so retry after the batch settles.
- A failed recipient whose counterparty account changed its address since the batch was sent is not paid either address: the retry returns `409 TRANSFER_BATCH_DESTINATION_CHANGED` naming it in `error.details.recipientIds`, and nothing is sent. Send that recipient in a new batch.
- A native SOL recipient paid less than the rent-exempt minimum at an address with no account fails again for the same reason, so the retry is refused with `409 AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM` and that recipient stays `failed`. Send it in a new batch with a larger amount.
- Only recipients that are still `failed` are ever sent, so a retry under a new key never pays anyone twice.

Never resend the whole batch under a new `Idempotency-Key` to finish it: that pays the recipients who already succeeded again.

### The SOL rent-exempt minimum

A Solana wallet holds either nothing or at least the rent-exempt minimum (about 0.00089 SOL), and the network refuses a native SOL transfer that would break that, along with every recipient in the same transaction. SDP checks before it sends:

- A recipient whose address has no account must receive at least the minimum.
- The source wallet must end with nothing or at least the minimum. Chunks land in any order, so a batch that sends the wallet's whole balance also needs every chunk to move at least the minimum.

`POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches/estimate` lists what would fail in `estimate.warnings` (`AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM` per recipient, `SOURCE_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM` for the source). `POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches` refuses the batch with `409 AMOUNT_BELOW_RENT_MINIMUM`, naming `details.recipientIndexes` and `details.sourceRemainder`, before anything is written or sent. The 409 is not stored under the `Idempotency-Key`, so the same request runs again once it would clear. Token batches are unaffected: SDP funds a missing token account's rent (`tokenAccountRentLamports`).

### Token account rent per transaction

SDP funds new recipient token accounts up to a per-transaction rent limit. A chunk includes only as many new accounts as that limit covers; existing accounts are packed by count and size. The estimate's `transactionCount` is the number of transactions create submits. If one account exceeds the limit, create is refused with `409 SPONSORED_RENT_OVER_CAP` (`details.recipientIndex`) before anything is written or sent. Create that token account first.

## Paying recipients one transfer at a time

To pay destinations that are not saved counterparty accounts, send one transfer per recipient instead of a batch:

1. **Resolve recipients** in your application: the rows to pay, each with a destination address and an amount.
2. **Pick a run id** you control, such as `payout_2026-05-14_marketplace_sellers`.
3. **Send** each recipient a `POST /v1/payments/transfers` with the destination, amount, token, and a memo that holds the run id and the row (`payout_2026-05-14_marketplace_sellers/row_4837`).
4. **Store** the returned transfer `id` and `status` with the recipient row, so you can read the status again later.
5. **Reconcile** once every row is sent: list `GET /v1/payments/transfers?direction=outbound&from=…&to=…` and check that every row has a matching `finalized` transfer.

Send transfers sequentially or in modest concurrency (4–8 in flight); high concurrency increases the chance of priority-fee contention and blockhash expiry without much throughput gain.

To tie a single transfer to a saved counterparty account, pass `counterpartyAccountId` with it. See [Pay a counterparty](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment#pay-a-counterparty).

### Dedup and retries for single transfers

Two layers keep a worker that dies mid-run from paying anyone twice:

1. **Idempotency keys**: `POST /v1/payments/transfers` requires an `Idempotency-Key`. Give each recipient row one stable key and reuse it for retries. A retry with the same key and request returns the original transfer. Reusing the key for a different request returns `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, and a retry while the original is still running returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT`.
2. **Application mapping**: store each row's transfer `id` before you move to the next row. On restart, retry with the row's same key, or skip rows that already have a transfer `id`.

A new key is a new payment, even with an identical body. The `signature` is unique across SDP transfers once set: use it to cross-check another indexer, not to retry.

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: payout-row-4837" \
  -d '{
    "sourceCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_123",
    "destination": "7xKXz...9fGh",
    "token": "9aBCd...4eEf",
    "amount": "150.00",
    "memo": "payout_2026-05-14_marketplace_sellers/row_4837"
  }'
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="payout-recipient.ts"
async function payoutRecipient(row: PayoutRow): Promise<string> {
  if (row.transferId) return row.transferId; // already submitted

  const response = await fetch(
    "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers",
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Authorization": "Bearer sf_...",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Idempotency-Key": row.idempotencyKey,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        sourceCustodyWalletId: row.sourceCustodyWalletId,
        destination: row.destination,
        token: row.token,
        amount: row.amount,
        memo: `${row.batchId}/row_${row.id}`,
      }),
    }
  );

  const { data } = await response.json();
  // The transfer record is under data.transfer (standard SDP success envelope).
  await row.persistTransferId(data.transfer.id); // persist BEFORE returning
  return data.transfer.id;
}
```

**Java**

```java title="PayoutRecipient.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sf_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .header("Idempotency-Key", idempotencyKey)
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "sourceCustodyWalletId": "%s",
          "destination": "%s",
          "token": "%s",
          "amount": "%s",
          "memo": "%s/row_%s"
        }""".formatted(sourceCustodyWalletId, destination, token, amount, batchId, rowId)))
    .build();
```

## Reconciling a run

After the loop finishes, list all outbound transfers in the run's time window and tally against your recipient table:

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers?direction=outbound&from=2026-05-14T00:00:00Z&to=2026-05-14T23:59:59Z&pageSize=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..."
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="list-outbound-transfers.ts"
async function* listOutboundTransfers(from: string, to: string) {
  let page = 1;
  while (true) {
    const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers");
    url.searchParams.set("direction", "outbound");
    url.searchParams.set("from", from);
    url.searchParams.set("to", to);
    url.searchParams.set("page", String(page));
    url.searchParams.set("pageSize", "100");

    const res = await fetch(url, {
      headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sf_..." },
    });
    const { data, meta } = await res.json();
    yield* data;
    if (!meta.hasMore) return;
    page += 1;
  }
}
```

To scope the list to one run, add `search=<run id>`, which matches part of the memo, or filter on `memo.startsWith(runId)` yourself. Match each recipient row by its transfer `id`.

## Failure modes

Handle these outcomes for each transfer:

- **`failed`**: the transfer never reached the network, or the network rejected it (insufficient funds, frozen account, expired blockhash). `error` says why. The recipient was not paid; to retry, send a new transfer with a new `Idempotency-Key`.
- **`processing` for longer than you expect**: the request stopped waiting before the chain settled the transfer. Read it with `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` instead of sending it again, and send a new transfer only once `status` is `failed`.
- **Mid-run worker crash**: resume with each row's original `Idempotency-Key`, and store the returned transfer `id` before you move on.
- **Fee sponsor unavailable**: SDP pays the network fee on every transfer it signs, so the source wallet never needs SOL for fees. When the sponsor can't pay, SDP refuses the transfer without charging the source wallet.

## Payments: Accept Payments

### Accept payments
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/accept-overview

> Get paid into a wallet you control, through a dashboard payment link or a shared address, and find each payment.

To accept a payment, the payer sends tokens to one of your custody wallets and you find that payment. Send a payment link from the dashboard, or share a wallet address and detect payments yourself. [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification) covers when a payment is final, and [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing) covers listing and matching.

## Payment requests

In the dashboard, open **Payments** > **Requests**, click **New**, and set the amount, token, destination wallet and when the link expires. You get a link and a Solana Pay QR code that anyone can pay, and SDP pays the network fee for the payer's transaction. Each request gets its own Solana Pay reference, which SDP watches to see when the request is paid.

When a request is paid, SDP records an inbound `finalized` transfer with `kind: request_deposit`, which `GET /v1/payments/transfers?direction=inbound` returns. Create one in the dashboard or with `POST /v1/payments/requests`, and cancel it with `POST /v1/payments/requests/{paymentRequestId}/cancel`.

## Share a wallet address

Give the payer a custody wallet's Solana address. Copy it from **Payments** > **Deposit**, or read `publicKey` from [`GET /v1/wallets/{walletId}`](/docs/reference/api/wallets) (add `includeBalance=false` to skip the balance read). The payer sends an ordinary SOL or SPL transfer from any wallet. To offer a QR code, build a Solana Pay URL from the address, token mint and amount yourself.

SDP does not record these payments. You see them through `GET /v1/payments/transfers` with that wallet's `custodyWalletId` and `includeObserved=true`, which reads the wallet's recent on-chain history. These observed rows carry no memo or reference, and they never reach `finalized`; see [Observed transfers](/docs/payments/accept-indexing#observed-transfers).

### Match payments to orders

An observed payment's on-record keys are the wallet it landed in and its `destination`. To tell payments apart, give each order (or each customer) its own receiving wallet. One wallet per merchant, seller or ledger account works when you don't need to match single payments, such as treasury or settlement flows. To correlate by memo or Solana Pay reference instead, read the transaction from Solana RPC by its `signature`.

## What SDP gives you

- **Payment links**: payment requests, from the dashboard or `POST /v1/payments/requests`, recorded as inbound transfers once paid.
- **Observed payments**: a wallet's recent on-chain activity, from `GET /v1/payments/transfers?custodyWalletId=…&includeObserved=true`. See [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing).
- **Status reads**: `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` for one recorded transfer. See [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification).
- **Balances**: `GET /v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/balances`, where `walletId` is the provider wallet id (`walletId` from `GET /v1/wallets`). See [Wallet balances](/docs/wallet-operations/balances).

## What SDP does not give you

- **No checkout or payment-intent API**: a payment request is the only object you create ahead of a payment. Match payments to a shared wallet address against the order records you keep.
- **No settlement webhooks**: poll for status. See [Polling cadence](/docs/payments/accept-verification#polling-cadence).

## Example: a marketplace checkout

A minimal accept flow on per-order wallets:

1. At checkout, create a custody wallet for the order, or take one from a pool you keep. Store its `id`, its `publicKey`, the token and the expected amount on your `orders` row.
2. Show the payer the address, token and amount, or a Solana Pay QR code you build from them.
3. The payer's wallet sends the transfer.
4. Your worker polls each open order's wallet with `custodyWalletId` and `includeObserved=true`, and looks for an inbound transfer whose `token` and `amount` fit the order. Observed reads have their own quota, so space the polls out.
5. Check with Solana RPC that the transfer's `signature` is `finalized`, then mark the order paid. Store the `signature` so a rerun of the worker never applies the payment twice.

Treat your `orders` table as the checkout state machine and SDP as the wallet and settlement backend.

## Next steps

- [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification): statuses, and when a payment is safe to act on.
- [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing): list transfers, dedupe, and run a polling worker.

### Verifying a payment
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/accept-verification

> Transfer statuses, finality on Solana, polling, and how to check a payment against the chain yourself.

A transfer's `status` tells you whether a payment landed and whether it can still be undone. This page covers each status, when a payment is safe to act on, and how to check it against the chain.

## Status lifecycle

A wallet transfer, sent or received, has one of these statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `processing` | Outbound and in flight: SDP is signing and submitting it, or waiting for the chain. `signature` can still be `null`. |
| `confirmed` | The transaction landed in a block that a supermajority of the cluster voted for. `signature` and `slot` are set. Not yet irreversible. |
| `finalized` | The block is finalized. Irreversible. |
| `failed` | The transfer never reached the network, or the network rejected it. The recipient was not paid; `error` says why. |

`POST /v1/payments/transfers` waits for finality, so a successful request usually answers `finalized`. If the wait runs out, it answers `processing`, and SDP moves the transfer to `confirmed`, `finalized` or `failed` as the chain settles. A `processing` transfer that never got a `signature` fails after 5 minutes, unless it is waiting on a custody approval.

Inbound payments differ. A paid payment request is recorded at `finalized`. An observed row (from `includeObserved=true`) shows `confirmed` or `failed` and never `finalized`, because SDP rebuilds it from chain history on each read. Check its finality yourself; see [Independent verification](#independent-verification).

`finalized` and `failed` are final. Transfers that other modules create document their own lifecycle.

## Finality on Solana

Act on `finalized` for anything irreversible: releasing custody, shipping high-value goods, posting to your general ledger. A `confirmed` transaction has a supermajority vote but can, rarely, still be dropped. Use it for low-stakes steps, such as a status email or a "paid" badge.

## Polling cadence

SDP sends no settlement webhooks, so poll:

- `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` for one recorded transfer.
- `GET /v1/payments/transfers` for a time window or one wallet's activity. See [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing).

Start from these ranges:

- **Active checkout** (someone is watching the payment screen): every 2–5 seconds for up to a minute, then back off.
- **Background reconciliation** (no one is waiting): every 15–30 seconds, or on each worker tick.
- **After the fact**: one read when your application needs the answer, with no loop.

Every poll counts against your key's [rate limit](/docs/reference/conventions/rate-limits). Reads with `includeObserved=true` also count against their own quota of 30 a minute per API key, so spread them across your open orders.

## Independent verification

Once a transfer has a `signature`, you can check it against the network yourself:

- **`signature`**: open it on [Solana Explorer](https://explorer.solana.com/), or look it up with `getSignatureStatuses` on your own RPC.
- **`slot`**: the slot the transaction landed in.
- **`blockTime`**: the block's timestamp (ISO 8601). It is often `null` on transfers SDP sends; `confirmedAt` records when SDP saw the transaction land.
- **`fee`**: the network fee in lamports, when known.

If you run your own indexer, compare its view of each `signature` with SDP's `status`.

## Failure handling

When `status` is `failed`:

- Read `error` for the reason.
- Decide whether to try again. The failed transfer stays failed, and its `Idempotency-Key` replays the failure. To retry, send a new request with a new key; it creates a new transfer with its own `id` and `signature`.
- Tell whoever needs to know: the merchant, the customer, your operations team.

- [Accept overview](/docs/payments/accept-overview): payment requests and shared addresses.
- [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing): list and match many transfers.
- [Concepts: the transfer data model](/docs/payments/concepts#the-transfer-data-model): every transfer field.

### Indexing and reconciliation
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/accept-indexing

> List transfers, read a wallet's observed payments, dedupe, and reconcile against your own ledger.

`GET /v1/payments/transfers` lists the transfers SDP has recorded in your project, including what you sent (single, batch and recurring) and paid payment requests. Filter by direction, status, token, wallet, counterparty and date. To also see payments SDP never recorded, such as a customer's direct transfer to your address, pass one wallet's `custodyWalletId` with `includeObserved=true`.

## Listing inbound transfers

The minimal inbound request:

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers?direction=inbound&pageSize=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..."
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="list-inbound-transfers.ts"
const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers");
url.searchParams.set("direction", "inbound");
url.searchParams.set("pageSize", "50");

const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sf_..." },
});
const { data, meta } = await res.json();
// data: Transfer[]
// meta: { total, page, pageSize, hasMore, requestId }
```

Without `includeObserved`, this returns recorded inbound transfers only, such as paid payment requests.

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `inbound` \| `outbound` | Inbound is a payment into one of your wallets. |
| `status` | string | One or more of `processing`, `confirmed`, `finalized`, `failed`, comma-separated. |
| `custodyWalletId` | string | One wallet's SDP `id` (`cwlt_…` from `GET /v1/wallets`). |
| `includeObserved` | boolean | Default `false`. With `custodyWalletId`, adds the wallet's recent on-chain activity; see [Observed transfers](#observed-transfers). |
| `token` | string | A well-known symbol (`SOL`, `USDC`) or a mint address. A well-known token matches either form. |
| `counterpartyId` | string | Transfers tied to one counterparty (`cpty_…`). |
| `search` | string | 3 or more characters, matched against ids, signatures, addresses, memo and counterparty names. |
| `from`, `to` | ISO 8601 datetime | Window on `createdAt`. Include a time zone, such as `2026-05-14T00:00:00Z`. |
| `sortBy`, `sortDirection` | string | Default `createdAt`, `desc`. |
| `page`, `pageSize` | integer | Default `1` and `20`. `pageSize` is at most `100`. |

[List transfers](/docs/reference/api/payments/list-payment-transfers) has every parameter.

## Observed transfers

With `custodyWalletId` and `includeObserved=true`, the list adds what the wallet's recent on-chain history shows and SDP has no record of:

- SDP builds these rows from the wallet's latest signatures (at most 200) on each read, and does not store them. Use them for recent activity, not history.
- Their `id` starts with `xfr_observed_`. It stays the same across reads, but `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` does not find it.
- `status` is `confirmed` or `failed`, never `finalized`. `custodyWalletId` is `null`, and there is no `memo`.
- Reads with `includeObserved=true` have their own quota: 30 a minute per API key and 120 per organization. Past it they return `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

## Deduplication

- **Recorded transfers**: key them by `id` (`xfr_…`), which exists before any `signature` does. Once set, `signature` is unique across SDP's recorded transfers, so it also dedupes against another chain indexer.
- **Observed rows**: key them by `id`, not `signature`. One transaction can produce more than one row.

## Reconciling an order

For a customer's direct payment, the on-record keys are the receiving wallet and `destination`: observed rows carry no memo or reference. Give each order its own receiving wallet (see [Accept payments](/docs/payments/accept-overview#match-payments-to-orders)), then for each open order:

1. **Read** every page of the wallet's inbound activity, while `meta.hasMore` is `true`: `GET /v1/payments/transfers?custodyWalletId=<cwlt_…>&includeObserved=true&direction=inbound&pageSize=100`.
2. **Match** a transfer whose `token` and `amount` fit the order.
3. **Check finality**: observed rows stop at `confirmed`, so check with Solana RPC (`getSignatureStatuses`) that the `signature` is `finalized` before any irreversible step.
4. **Apply** the payment once: mark the order paid, store the `signature`, and start downstream work (email, shipment, ledger entry).
5. **Leave unmatched transfers** for the next pass, or flag them for review after a grace period.

A paid payment request needs none of this: SDP records it as an inbound `finalized` transfer.

## A polling worker

A worker that checks each open order's wallet on every tick:

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="reconcile-tick.ts"
// Observed reads have their own quota (30 a minute per API key), and each
// page is one read. Past it, the worker waits out Retry-After and reads the
// same page again, so no order is skipped.
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function reconcileTick(openOrders: Order[]) {
  orders: for (const order of openOrders) {
    let page = 1;
    while (true) {
      const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers");
      url.searchParams.set("custodyWalletId", order.custodyWalletId);
      url.searchParams.set("includeObserved", "true");
      url.searchParams.set("direction", "inbound");
      url.searchParams.set("pageSize", "100");
      url.searchParams.set("page", String(page));

      const res = await fetch(url, {
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}` },
      });
      if (res.status === 429) {
        await sleep(Number(res.headers.get("Retry-After")) * 1000);
        continue; // the same page again
      }
      const { data, meta } = await res.json();

      for (const tr of data) {
        if (tr.status === "failed" || (await alreadyApplied(tr.id))) continue;
        if (tr.token !== order.mint || !sameAmount(tr.amount, order.amount)) continue;
        // Observed rows stop at "confirmed": check finality with your own RPC.
        if (!(await isFinalized(tr.signature))) continue;
        await markOrderPaid(order, tr); // stores tr.id and tr.signature
        continue orders; // paid: apply it once, then move to the next order
      }
      if (!meta.hasMore) break;
      page++;
    }
  }
}
```

Stop polling an order's wallet once the order is paid or expired, so the quota goes to open orders. `sameAmount` compares decimal strings by value: `"100"` and `"100.00"` are the same amount.

## Payments: Ramps

### Ramps
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps

> Discover corridors, estimate a rate, quote a ramp, and hand the customer to the provider to complete it.

A **Ramp Quote** moves money between fiat and crypto through a ramp provider. SDP prices it with the provider when you ask, opens a **Payment Transfer** for it, and hands your customer to the provider's own flow (a hosted page or an embedded session) to complete it. SDP then tracks the provider's reports and verifies the crypto leg on chain.

Every quote names a **Counterparty**, the customer the provider runs KYC on, and a custody wallet you control. Provider configuration and capabilities are on [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers).

## Prerequisites

1. **A Counterparty.** Create one with `POST /v1/counterparties`.
2. **The provider's requirements met**, if it has any. Some providers need KYC or bank details collected against the counterparty before they price or accept a quote. Read `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/requirements` with the quote's `provider`, `direction`, `assetRail`, and `fiatCurrency`, plus `destinationCustodyWalletId` for an onramp. While `status` is `collect`, send what it lists with `POST` to the same path. Quote once it's `ready`.
3. **A custody wallet you control**, for the crypto leg: the onramp destination or the offramp source.

## Discovering corridors

`GET /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency` and `GET /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` list the fiat and crypto pairs SDP supports, and the providers that cover each one. Which fiat currencies work depends on the provider and the asset, so check here rather than assume.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency?source=USD&dest=usdc.solana" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..."
```

| Query param | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | Onramp: fiat currency (ISO code). Offramp: crypto rail (`usdc.solana`, `sol.solana`, …). |
| `dest` | Onramp: crypto rail. Offramp: fiat currency. |
| `provider` | Narrow to one provider. |

`pairs` lists the providers for each source and destination. `providerDetails` gives each provider's support for the direction: amount limits per currency, country coverage, and the entity types it accepts.

## Estimating a rate

`POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/estimate` and `POST /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/estimate` preview a rate without creating anything, and need no counterparty or wallet. SDP asks every provider on the corridor and returns one entry per provider in `estimates`. An onramp estimate takes `fiatAmount`; an offramp estimate takes `cryptoAmount`.

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/estimate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
    "fiatCurrency": "USD",
    "fiatAmount": "100.00"
  }'
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="estimate-onramp.ts"
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/estimate",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sf_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      assetRail: "usdc.solana",
      fiatCurrency: "USD",
      fiatAmount: "100.00",
    }),
  }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.estimates: one entry per provider on the corridor
```

Each entry has a `status`:

- `ok`: `estimate` carries `fiatAmount`, `cryptoAmount`, `exchangeRate`, and `fees`, plus `totalFiatAmount` on an onramp. Show it to the customer before they commit to a quote.
- `unsupported`: the provider gives no estimate here. Its rate is known only at quote time.
- `error`: the provider call failed or was refused. An amount outside the provider's range carries `reason` (`amount_below_minimum` or `amount_above_maximum`) and the `limit`.

## Requesting a quote

`POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` (fiat to crypto) and `POST /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/quote` (crypto to fiat) create the **Ramp Quote** with the provider you name. Unlike an estimate, a quote needs a counterparty and a wallet, and it opens a record at the provider. The request is the same for every provider: only `provider` changes. A pair the provider doesn't cover returns `400 UNSUPPORTED_CORRIDOR`, with the providers that do in `details.supportedProviders`.

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal" rotate-providers
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "moonpay",
    "counterpartyId": "cpty_...",
    "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
    "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
    "fiatCurrency": "USD",
    "fiatAmount": "100.00"
  }'
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript title="onramp-quote.ts" rotate-providers
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sf_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      provider: "moonpay",
      counterpartyId: "cpty_...",
      destinationCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_...",
      assetRail: "usdc.solana",
      fiatCurrency: "USD",
      fiatAmount: "100.00",
    }),
  }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.quote.deliveryMode says how to hand off; data.transferId names the transfer to follow
```

**Python**

```python title="onramp_quote.py" rotate-providers
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sf_..."},
    json={
        "provider": "moonpay",
        "counterpartyId": "cpty_...",
        "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
        "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
        "fiatCurrency": "USD",
        "fiatAmount": "100.00",
    },
)
data = response.json()["data"]
```

### Request fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | yes | A provider from the [capability matrix](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#capability-matrix). |
| `counterpartyId` | yes | An existing Counterparty. SDP resolves the provider's customer and payout records from it, so you don't send them. |
| `destinationCustodyWalletId` (onramp) / `sourceCustodyWalletId` (offramp) | yes | The `id` of a custody wallet you control, as `GET /v1/wallets` returns it. It must be in your API key's wallet scope. |
| `assetRail` | yes | SDP's crypto asset rail: `usdc.solana`, `usdt.solana`, `sol.solana`, and so on. |
| `fiatCurrency` | onramp: yes; offramp: no | Required on an onramp. On an offramp, the provider's default applies when you leave it out (see its page). |
| `fiatAmount` (onramp) / `cryptoAmount` (offramp) | yes | A decimal string greater than zero. |
| `rampsMemo` | no | Up to 20 key/value string pairs (keys up to 64 characters, values up to 256), stored on the transfer for your own reconciliation. |

### The response

The response holds `quote` and `transferId`, the **Payment Transfer** the quote opened. Follow the ramp with [`GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}`](/docs/reference/api/payments/get-payment-transfer). `quote.status` is always `pending`: SDP never updates a quote, so the transfer is what moves. There's no endpoint to read a quote again.

`quote.deliveryMode` says how to hand the customer to the provider:

| Delivery mode | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `hosted` | Redirect the customer to `quote.hostedUrl`. |
| `session_widget` | Mount the provider's session with `quote.clientSecret` and `quote.publishableKey`. |

Each provider's delivery mode is in the [capability matrix](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#capability-matrix). An onramp needs nothing more from you: the provider delivers to the wallet, and SDP completes the transfer once it verifies the delivery on chain.

## Funding an offramp

An offramp needs one more call, because you send the crypto. When the provider is ready for it, the transfer moves to `awaiting_payment` and carries `cryptoDeposit`, with the `destinationAddress` and `amount` to send.

Send exactly that with [`POST /v1/payments/transfers`](/docs/reference/api/payments/create-payment-transfer). Set `transferId` to the offramp's transfer, `sourceCustodyWalletId` to the quote's source wallet, `destination` and `amount` from `cryptoDeposit`, and `token` to the quoted asset (its symbol, such as `USDC`, or its mint). The call needs an `Idempotency-Key`, like any transfer, and your API key needs `transfers.execute`.

A deposit that doesn't match the instruction returns `400`, and one for a transfer no longer awaiting payment returns `409`. Sending the same deposit again, under any key, returns the transfer it already funded instead of sending twice.

## Canceling a quote

`POST /v1/payments/ramps/transfers/cancel` cancels the transfer behind a quote while it's still `pending` or `awaiting_payment`, before the customer has paid. Your API key needs `ramp_transfers.manage`.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/transfers/cancel \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "transferId": "xfr_..." }'
```

A transfer in any other status returns `400` instead. If its status changes while you cancel, you get `409`. Canceling a canceled transfer returns it again.

## Transfer status

Each quote's **Payment Transfer** has its own lifecycle, apart from wallet transfers ([Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification)):

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The quote opened the transfer. The customer hasn't paid yet. |
| `awaiting_payment` | The provider is waiting for payment. On an offramp, `cryptoDeposit` says what to send. |
| `processing` | Offramp only: SDP is sending your crypto deposit. |
| `settling` | The provider is processing the ramp, or reported it settled and SDP is verifying it on chain. An offramp also waits here for the provider's payout once its deposit lands. |
| `completed` | Onramp: SDP verified on chain that the quoted asset reached the wallet. Offramp: SDP's deposit is finalized and the provider reported the fiat payout. |
| `canceled` | Canceled with `POST /v1/payments/ramps/transfers/cancel` before payment. |
| `expired` | The checkout lapsed unpaid: the provider expired it, or SDP did after no provider activity. |
| `failed` | The quote failed, the provider rejected or reversed the ramp, or the offramp deposit failed. `error` says why, when set. |

`completed`, `failed`, and `canceled` are final. An `expired` transfer comes back if the provider reports progress, for example when the customer completes an earlier checkout.

A provider's settlement report alone never completes a transfer: missing or mismatched chain evidence keeps it `settling` for review. On an offramp, the fiat payout stays the provider's report, because chain finality proves the crypto deposit, not the bank credit.

## Rate limits

Estimates and quotes have quotas of their own, counted per key (or signed-in member) and per organization. Onramp and offramp share each one. While SDP's counter store is unavailable, both refuse with `503` rather than run uncounted.

| Endpoint | Per key | Per organization |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.../estimate` | 30 / minute | 120 / minute |
| `.../quote` | 20 / minute | 60 / minute |

## Choosing a provider

Always pass `provider`: SDP doesn't pick one for you. Choose by:

- **Availability:** the providers your organization can use. See [Provider gating](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#provider-gating).
- **Corridor:** currency, country, and entity type, from the currency endpoints above.
- **Environment:** your project's environment picks the provider's sandbox or production mode. See [Sandbox vs production selection](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#sandbox-vs-production-selection).

## Related

- [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers): provider configuration and the capability matrix.
- [Accept payments](/docs/payments/accept-overview): how inbound transfers show up.

### Ramp providers
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps-providers

> The capability matrix, sandbox and production selection, and provider availability for SDP ramp providers.

SDP integrates the ramp providers in the matrix below. The SDP API deployment configures each one with environment variables, and the `provider` field on a quote picks between them.

## Sandbox vs production selection

The project's environment picks the mode for every request: a Sandbox project uses a provider's sandbox credentials, a Production project its production ones. Each key is named `<PROVIDER>_<MODE>_<ROLE>`, with `MODE` either `SANDBOX` or `PRODUCTION`. A provider whose keys for a mode are missing, or are the other mode's, answers `503 PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` in that mode. A deployment can configure any subset of providers. Each provider's page lists the keys it reads.

## Capability matrix

| Provider | Onramp | Offramp | Sandbox | Delivery mode | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [MoonPay](/docs/payments/ramps-moonpay) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `hosted` | Fast sandbox iteration; broad payment-method coverage (corridor-dependent). |
| [Stripe](/docs/payments/ramps-stripe) | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ (shared credentials) | `session_widget` | Widget/session-embedded onramp UI; onramp only. |

Each provider's page covers its configuration and limits. The **Best for** column compares the providers this deployment offers.

## Provider gating

A provider is usable when its **Provider Availability** allows it: the deployment configures it, and the organization may use it. Ramp providers are generally available, so every organization can use a configured one unless the deployment's operator turns it off for that organization.

SDP checks this on every estimate and quote. A quote with a provider the organization can't use returns `403 FORBIDDEN`, and `details.reason` says why: `provider_not_in_release_channel`, `provider_not_offered`, or `provider_not_entitled`. An estimate reports the refusal in that provider's entry instead.

## Become a ramp provider

Ramp integrations follow the [provider onboarding](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding) process, with their own intake and criteria:

| Category | Intake form | Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ramp | [Complete ramp intake](https://solanafoundation.typeform.com/to/sxTGbwXt) | [Download ramp criteria PDF](/provider-onboarding/ramp-criteria.pdf) |

## Related

- [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps): the onramp and offramp endpoints and their requests.
- [Provider onboarding](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding): how a provider joins SDP.

### MoonPay
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps-moonpay

> Configure MoonPay as an SDP ramp provider, with its credentials, capabilities, and limits.

MoonPay is one of SDP's ramp providers, for onramps and offramps. Its capabilities sit beside the others' in the [capability matrix](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#capability-matrix). Quote through [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps) with `"provider": "moonpay"`.

A Sandbox project uses the `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_*` keys, and a Production project the `MOONPAY_PRODUCTION_*` keys. MoonPay runs in a mode only while all three of that mode's keys are set and fit it. Otherwise it answers `PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_API_KEY` | Test-mode publishable key (`pk_test_…`). A live key is refused before any request. |
| `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY` | Test-mode secret key (`sk_test_…`). It signs the onramp and offramp widget URLs. |
| `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Test-mode webhook key (`wk_test_…`) that signs MoonPay's calls to `/webhooks/payments/ramps/sandbox/moonpay`. |
| `MOONPAY_PRODUCTION_API_KEY` | Live publishable key (`pk_live_…`). A test-mode key is refused before any request. |
| `MOONPAY_PRODUCTION_SECRET_KEY` | Live secret key (`sk_live_…`). |
| `MOONPAY_PRODUCTION_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Live webhook key (`wk_live_…`) that signs MoonPay's calls to `/webhooks/payments/ramps/production/moonpay`. |

## Behavior

- Quotes return `deliveryMode: "hosted"`: send the customer to `quote.hostedUrl`.
- An offramp quote without `fiatCurrency` pays out in `USD`.
- An offramp quote checks the source wallet's balance first, and refuses a sale the wallet can't fund with `400 INSUFFICIENT_TOKEN_BALANCE`.
- Send SDP's asset rails, such as `usdc.solana`. SDP maps them to MoonPay's currency codes, such as `usdc_sol`.

---

### Stripe
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps-stripe

> Configure Stripe as an SDP ramp provider, with its credentials, capabilities, and limits.

Stripe is one of SDP's ramp providers, for onramps only. Its capabilities sit beside the others' in the [capability matrix](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#capability-matrix). Quote through [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps) with `"provider": "stripe"`.

A Sandbox project uses the `STRIPE_SANDBOX_*` keys, and a Production project the `STRIPE_PRODUCTION_*` keys. Stripe runs in a mode only while all three of that mode's keys are set and fit it. Otherwise it answers `PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `STRIPE_SANDBOX_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Test-mode publishable key (`pk_test_…`), returned on the quote so your client can mount the onramp session. |
| `STRIPE_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY` | Test-mode secret key (`sk_test_…`, or a restricted `rk_test_…`). A live key is refused before any request. |
| `STRIPE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Signing secret (`whsec_…`) of the endpoint Stripe calls at `/webhooks/payments/ramps/sandbox/stripe`. A signed event with `livemode: true` is refused. |
| `STRIPE_PRODUCTION_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Live publishable key (`pk_live_…`). |
| `STRIPE_PRODUCTION_SECRET_KEY` | Live secret key (`sk_live_…`, or a restricted `rk_live_…`). A test-mode key is refused before any request. |
| `STRIPE_PRODUCTION_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Signing secret of the endpoint Stripe calls at `/webhooks/payments/ramps/production/stripe`. A signed event with `livemode: false` is refused. |

## Behavior

- Onramp only: an offramp quote naming Stripe returns `400 UNSUPPORTED_CORRIDOR`.
- An onramp buys `usdc.solana` or `sol.solana` with `USD`, for individuals in the US.
- Quotes return `deliveryMode: "session_widget"`, with `clientSecret`, `sessionId`, and `publishableKey` to mount Stripe's crypto onramp session, plus an optional `redirectUrl`.

## Tokens

### Tokenize an Asset
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/tokenize-an-asset

> Map a real-world asset to the right SDP token model, authorities, and implementation flow.

Issue a stablecoin, a tokenized security, a loyalty token or any other asset through SDP. This page takes you from choosing a model to your first API call.

## Choose a token model

Pick the **Tokenization Template** that matches the asset's compliance and operating needs:

| Asset model | Template | Default controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fiat-backed stablecoin | `stablecoin` | Freeze, pause, permanent delegate, blocklist |
| Tokenized security or RWA | `tokenized-security` | Freeze, pause, permanent delegate, allowlist |
| Loyalty, rewards or utility token | `custom` | Extensions you choose |
| Any other asset | `custom` | Extensions you choose |

At deploy, SDP gives every authority to the custody wallet that signs the deploy, unless you assign other custody wallets. While a custody wallet holds an authority, SDP signs the operations that authority controls, with no external signing. [Tokenization Templates](/docs/reference/issuance-token-types) lists each template's defaults.

## Compliance enforced onchain

Token-2022 extensions make compliance enforceable onchain. Freeze one holder's account, pause the token, seize or force-burn tokens, and manage the token's **Token Access Control** list. Freeze takes a `reason`; seize and force burn take a `memo`. Every token operation is one `POST` on the token:

**JavaScript**

```javascript title="compliance-action.js" rotate-token-ops
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sf_...",
      "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID(),
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(operationParams),
  },
);
const result = await response.json();
```

**Python**

```python title="compliance_action.py" rotate-token-ops
import requests
import uuid

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sf_...", "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
    json=operation_params,
)
result = response.json()
```

**curl**

```bash title="Terminal" rotate-token-ops
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$OPERATION_PARAMS"
```

## Audit trail

SDP records every issuance and compliance action in its audit log. Read one token's history with `GET /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/audit`, or on the token's **Activity** tab in the dashboard.

| Area | Recorded events |
| --- | --- |
| Token issuance | Create, edit, deploy, mint, burn, supply refresh and authority updates |
| Compliance | Freeze, unfreeze, pause, unpause, seize, force burn and access list changes |
| Asset profiles | Profile create, edit and delete |

## Idempotency

The calls that sign and send (deploy, mint, burn, force burn, freeze, unfreeze, pause, unpause, seize and authority updates) take an `Idempotency-Key` ([Idempotency](/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency)). A retry with the same key and body replays the first result instead of running again.

Issuance keys share one namespace across every operation and token in your organization. Reusing a key for a different request, even on another token, returns `409`. Create, edit and access list calls take no key.

## Implementation sequence

Each step links to its guide, with dashboard and API instructions:

1. [Set up your organization and projects](/docs/guides/setup-organization)
2. [Create a wallet](/docs/guides/setup-wallets)
3. [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys)
4. [Create a token](/docs/tokens/create-a-token)
5. [Deploy a token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token)
6. [Mint and burn](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn)
7. [Send a basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment): transfer tokens between wallets
8. [Allowlists](/docs/tokens/allowlists): the access list, on by default for `tokenized-security`
9. [Freeze and compliance](/docs/tokens/freeze-and-compliance): screen, freeze, pause and seize
10. [Manage token settings](/docs/tokens/manage-token-settings): move or revoke authorities and edit metadata

## Core API endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/templates` | List token templates |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens` | Create a token draft |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy` | Deploy to Solana |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/mint` | Mint new supply |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/burn` | Reduce supply |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist` | Add an address to the access list |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/freeze` | Freeze an account |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/pause` | Pause all transfers |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/transfers` | Transfer tokens |

See the full schemas in the [Issuance API reference](/docs/reference/api/issuance) and the [Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments).

## Operational constraints

- Create a token before you deploy it, and deploy it before you mint or transfer it.
- While a token is paused, SDP refuses mint, burn, seize and force burn with `400 TOKEN_PAUSED`, and the pausable extension stops transfers onchain.
- Freeze and unfreeze take a holder's wallet address; SDP finds the token account.
- SDP signs only with authorities that a custody wallet in the project holds. An operation whose authority no custody wallet holds returns `409`. If an authority moves to a wallet outside SDP custody, its holder has to move it back.

Driving SDP from an agent? Start from [Documentation for AI](/docs/reference/docs-for-ai), which links the machine-readable discovery files grounded in the public API.

### Create a Token
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/create-a-token

> Define a new token using a template or custom configuration.

Creating a token saves its metadata, extensions and rules in SDP as a draft (`status: "pending"`). Nothing reaches Solana until you [deploy it](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token).

![Empty Issuance page with a Create a draft button](/images/tokens/token-list-empty.png)

## Before you begin

- A custody wallet in the project ([Create a wallet](/docs/guides/setup-wallets)). The dashboard needs one to hold each key.
- For the API, a key with the `issuance.manage` grant.

## Templates

| Template | Decimals | Extensions | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stablecoin` | 6 | Permanent delegate, pausable | Fiat-backed tokens |
| `tokenized-security` | 8 | Permanent delegate, pausable, optional scaled UI amount; allowlist on by default | Regulated assets |
| `custom` | 9 | None until you add them | Full control |

The dashboard creates `stablecoin` tokens (**Stablecoin**) and `custom` tokens (**Non-security digital token**). Create a `tokenized-security` token through the API.

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Choose a template">

The template fixes the token's extensions and defaults. You review them before you create the draft.

<StepPanel>

**UI**

Open **Issuance** in the sidebar and click **Create a draft**. The flow has five steps.

On **What is this token?**, enter a **Name**, then choose a classification:

- **Stablecoin**: a token meant to hold a value, with freeze and pause switched on
- **Non-security digital token**: everything else, such as points, credits or tickets

Click **Continue**.

<img src="/docs/images/tokens/token-create-templates.png" alt="What is this token? step with the name Acme Dollar and Stablecoin selected" width="693" height="484" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto", margin: "0 0 18px" }} />

**API**

List the templates to see what each one sets:

```bash
curl 'https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDP_API_KEY"
```

```typescript
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDP_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

Pass a template's `id` as `template` when you create the token. Without `template`, the token is `custom`.

</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Set the token details">

Set the name, symbol and decimals. Symbol and decimals lock with the mint at deploy.

<StepPanel>

**UI**

On **Token details**, fill in:

- **Symbol**: up to 10 letters and digits, such as `ACME`
- **Decimals**: a stablecoin uses 6; other tokens start at 9
- **Description** and **Maximum supply** (optional; leave the cap empty for no cap)
- **Issuer name**: the legal entity issuing the token
- **Currency** (optional)

Click **Continue**.

<img src="/docs/images/tokens/token-create-identity.png" alt="Token details step with symbol ACME, 6 decimals, a description, issuer name and currency" width="693" height="679" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto", margin: "0 0 18px" }} />

**API**

Send the details to `POST /v1/issuance/tokens`:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Acme Dollar",
    "symbol": "ACME",
    "decimals": 6,
    "description": "USD-backed stablecoin",
    "template": "stablecoin"
  }'
```

`uri` is optional: an `http` or `https` URL of your metadata JSON. Without it, SDP serves the token's metadata JSON at `GET /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/metadata.json` and writes that URL onchain at deploy.

</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Choose controls and key holders">

Decide what the token can do and which wallet holds each of its keys.

<StepPanel>

**UI**

On **What this token can do**, choose the controls: **Freezable**, **Pausable**, **Permanent delegate**, **Access list** and **Mintable**. A stablecoin keeps all of them on, and its **Access list** is a blocklist or an allowlist. Any other token can turn them off, except **Mintable**, which is always on.

<img src="/docs/images/tokens/token-create-settings.png" alt="What this token can do step with every control on and Access list set to Allowlist" width="693" height="594" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto", margin: "0 0 18px" }} />

On **Who holds the keys**, choose a wallet for **Mint authority** (it also signs the deploy), **Metadata authority** and, when the token has them, **Freeze authority** and **Permanent delegate**.

<img src="/docs/images/tokens/token-create-keys.png" alt="Who holds the keys step with the Treasury wallet holding every authority" width="693" height="360" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%", height: "auto", margin: "0 0 18px" }} />

**API**

Add the controls to the same body. `signingCustodyWalletId` is the SDP wallet `id` from `GET /v1/wallets` (`cwlt_…`), not the provider's `walletId` or the wallet's public key. It's optional on create; you can set it at deploy. `isMintable` and `isFreezable` default to `true`.

```typescript title="create-token.ts"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: "Bearer sf_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    name: "Acme Dollar",
    symbol: "ACME",
    decimals: 6,
    description: "USD-backed stablecoin",
    template: "stablecoin",
    signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
    requiresAllowlist: false,
    isMintable: true,
    isFreezable: true,
  }),
});
```

For a custom token, set `template` to `"custom"` (or omit it) and pass `overrides.extensions`:

```typescript title="create-custom-token.ts"
body: JSON.stringify({
  name: "Game Coin",
  symbol: "GAME",
  decimals: 0,
  template: "custom",
  signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
  overrides: {
    extensions: {
      pausable: {},
      transferFee: { basisPoints: 50, maxFee: "1000" },
    },
  },
  isMintable: true,
  isFreezable: false,
}),
```

The signing wallet gets every authority unless you assign other custody wallets with `authorityCustodyWalletIds` [at deploy](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token).

</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Create the draft">

SDP stores the token with status `pending`. Nothing is written to Solana yet.

<StepPanel>

**UI**

On **Review**, check the draft and click **Create draft**. The **Draft created** toast confirms it, and the token's page opens in the **Draft** state.

**Save and exit** stores a complete draft in SDP. An unfinished one stays in this browser, under **Unfinished drafts** on Issuance.

![Issuance list with Acme Dollar marked Draft](/images/tokens/token-list-draft.png)

The draft's **Overview** tab holds **Deploy token**, the next step.

![Acme Dollar's Overview tab in the Draft state, with Deploy this token and its Deploy token button](/images/tokens/token-detail-pending.png)

**API**

A `201` response returns the token:

```typescript title="create-token.ts"
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.token.id: keep it for every later call
// data.token.status: "pending"
// data.token.signingCustodyWalletId: the wallet selected for deployment
```

Pass `data.token.id` to [Deploy a Token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token).

</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>
